His dog Bubbles was lounging on the couch, gnawing on his morning bone like always, when Mydei suddenly stormed out of the bathroom. He slammed a positive pregnancy test down on the table in front of Phainon, who started to choke. Bubbles perks up at the commotion and barks in alarm. “Is this–?”

“I took four more tests in the bathroom if you want to check. They all came back positive,” Mydei paused, sighed heavily before looking down at Bubbles, who was now pawing at his leg for attention. He bent down and gave the pooch a scratch behind the ear before straightening back up. “Look, I still gotta get back and feed Leo and open the cafe. We’ll have to talk about this later. See ya.” 

“Mydei, wait–” The blonde practically ran out of the apartment before Phainon could stop him. He then sat there silently and stared down at the test before him. 

A baby, Mydei’s pregnant with his—no, their baby. 

Bubbles whined pathetically and trotted over to lie down at the door, patiently waiting for Mydei to return despite Phainon being the one who rescued him from the shelter and gave him a home (traitor). 

Phainon got up and threw the rest of his breakfast into the trash, his appetite now completely gone. He went to the bathroom and spotted the tests lined up neatly on the toilet tank cover. It’s faint, but the second line is on all four. He threw them away in the trash before taking a seat on the closed lid of the toilet and putting his head in his hands.

He and Mydei have a simple no-strings-attached fuckbuddies type of relationship. A baby was not supposed to be a part of that equation. All the times they slept together, both men made sure to practice safe sex with either condoms or other contraceptives. Getting pregnant was never a goal, but it still happened. And Phainon feels immense guilt for feeling a little excited about the news. 

He’s been in love with Mydei for years, starting from when they first met at a house party as college freshmen. He saw the handsome Kremnoan leaning up against the wall with a drink in his hand, scowling daggers at any poor being that dared to cross his path. When Phainon first approached him with a simple question about what he was drinking, Mydei barked that he wasn’t interested. Dejected but still determined, Phainon waited before coming back with an offering of ice cream and cookies someone had baked for the party. 

That had been the crucial key for Mydei to open up. After begrudgingly taking the desserts, the two talked the whole night. Phainon learned that he was a library science major with a culinary minor, has a soft spot for his mother, animals, children, and a preference for sweets. They exchanged numbers by the end of the night and texted often, becoming close friends and even workout buddies after they ran into each other at the same gym. 

Phainon had since kept his more amorous feelings buried deep within, simply content to just be friends, when one night, after his last exam, Mydei bumped into him in their dormitory lobby. He looked rough, more haggard and tense than usual. When Phainon asked what was wrong, Mydei spared no details: “I’ve been so pent up I feel like I’m going to explode,” Mydei growled shamelessly when asked, his golden feline eyes scalding hot as they traveled down Phainon’s built body. 

The next thing he remembered was waking up to Mydei riding him with a cocky grin before coming vigorously all over Phainon’s chest. They spent the rest of the day wrapped up in each other. Phainon was pretty sure his entire floor hated him for that. But it eventually became a routine. When they moved into an off-campus apartment together and continued their relationship, Mydei established the ground rules about how to keep things platonic, specifically no kissing on the lips. It hurt tremendously at first, and it only got worse when Mydei went on dates with a few other people before suddenly stopping.

When he asked the blonde about it, Mydei just shrugged his shoulders. “Sometimes things just change.” Phainon tried not to find too much hope in that statement and continued to enjoy the time he had with his friend until they graduated and moved out. Mydei inherited a small cafe and bookstore from his mother, while Phainon found work as a physiotherapist at a nearby rehabilitation clinic. It didn’t stop them from catching up and occasionally falling into bed together. Phainon had been thrilled, now that they were a little older, he could finally confess his feelings for Mydei and maybe, just maybe…

Bubbles broke him out of his stupor with a paw on his lap, whining for Phainon’s attention this time. “Oh, now you want me,” he teased the pup with a small smile, giving him a scratch on the head between his fluffy ears. Despite his large size, Bubbles clambered up into Phainon’s lap, or at least tried to, resting his front legs on Phainon’s leg and leaning against the man’s chest. Phainon chuckled and petted the dog’s thick, fluffy white fur.

“What am I going to do?” he mumbled. Bubbles, of course, didn't answer and just licked Phainon’s nose.

You might want to check on whatever you have in the oven, because I think it’s starting to–” Mydei turned back to see the dark fumes starting to billow out from where he was baking his honeycake. He cursed and quickly opened the door, only to be assaulted by a thick plume of dark smoke. The baker coughed and hacked as he hastily grabbed the pan and threw the now ruined dessert onto the stovetop. “...burn.”

Mydei groaned and glared at the now unsalvageable mess before throwing it in the trash. The roots of a migraine already formed at his temple as the acidic scent of burnt sugar and butter refused to leave the kitchen. He felt like throwing up again. "Why don’t you go sit down outside and get some water? I’ll clean this up.” Hephaestion, his dear childhood friend, offered with a patient smile. Too tired and defeated to argue, Mydei sighed and allowed himself to be ushered out of the kitchen. He abstained the urge to hold his stomach as he stumbled over to the empty booth by the large store window where Leo was sunbathing on the windowsill like the lazy fuck he was. 

The feline cracked open one eye and let out a sleepy yawn before getting up to lounge across Mydei’s lap. He chuckled and gave the cat a scratch under the chin, feeling the thunderous purr vibrate through his fingers. Leo curled up against his midsection for a nap. He wondered if his cat had always known. 

A baby. An actual, living, breathing baby. A person he and Phainon created. He should have realized sooner, looking back at all the strangeness, that Mydei should have expected something amiss. But they had been so careful in all their years of casual sex that the thought of accidental pregnancy hadn’t crossed his mind as often as it should have. Mydei scrubbed his face with his hands, muffling the groan that slipped from his mouth. 

It was still early enough for Mydei to safely terminate the pregnancy. The decision was completely up to him, but the thought of getting rid of his–of their–baby made his heart twist. He tried to imagine what it would look like in a few months when the baby would start to show. Would they look like Phainon, with snowy white hair and piercing blue eyes, or more like Mydei? 

“Here,” Hephaestion finally emerges from the kitchen and sits across from him at the table. He held a cup of steaming hot tea in one hand and a large slice of oak cake, both placed in front of Mydei. Leo stirred awake from his nap and hopped off Mydei’s lap to wander off to the bookshelves.

“I’m not hungry,” Mydei lied. His friend just shot him an unimpressed arch of his eyebrow and pushed the dishes closer to him. Realizing that Hephaestion wouldn’t give up, Mydei sighed and took the smallest bite of the cake. He doesn’t normally like oak cakes, finding them a little tasteless and bland, but when it hit his tongue, Mydei was greatly surprised.

The sponge was so light that it melted on his tongue, and the oak syrup was fragrant and sweet. He quickly devoured and washed it down with the lemon tea. Mydei pointedly ignored the smug grin on Hephaestion’s face as he swiped up the last of the crumbs and shoveled them into his mouth. “Feeling better now?”

“Shut up,” Mydei grumbled, his cheeks flushed pink with embarrassment. For a moment, neither man spoke. Hephaestion silently studied him while Mydei looked everywhere but at him, his hands itching to touch his stomach again.

“So–” the long-haired brunette finally broke the silence, his voice kind and patient. “Are you gonna tell me what’s going on with you?” Mydei did his best not to let his anxiety and fear show too much on his face.

“I have no idea what you’re talking about. Nothing is going on,” fibbed Mydei. 

“And Perdikkas just told me he’s dropping out of medical school,” Hephaestion scoffs and crosses his arms over his chest. “Seriously, Mydeimos, what’s going on? You’ve been making silly mistakes in the kitchen, forgetting where you put things, staring off into space, and burning the pastries. Is everything okay? You know you can tell me anything. Is it your dad? Did something happen back at home?” The genuine concern in his friend’s voice, in his expression, sent a sharp pang of guilt through Mydei’s heart. He forcefully blinked them back and shook his head.

“Is there anything I can do to help?” 

Not unless you can turn back time to stop me and Phainon from sleeping together, Mydei thought to himself with bitter humor. He sighed, shoulders shagging as he finally gave in, fixing his closest friend with a determined look. 

“I’m pregnant.” The silence that followed was long and awkward. Hephaestion’s mouth fell slightly agape with surprise; his dark eyes were wide. Mydei shuffled around, unable to meet the other’s gaze. The urge to vomit slowly began to come up again. 

“Are you serious? You’re not messing with me?” Hephaestion demanded, forcing Mydei to laugh bitterly. 

“When have I ever been known to make jokes like this?” he asked rhetorically. 

“Sorry, I didn’t mean it that way,” Hephaestion coughed clumsily before scratching his head. “Are you sure it’s not a false positive? Those can happen sometimes.” Mydei shook his head and retold him the same thing he told Phainon. His childhood friend inhaled sharply, dark eyes quickly scanning and studying Mydei’s expression. “Oh, then I guess congratulations? Or my condolences? I don’t know what your plan for this is.” 

“I—” Mydei paused, his hand now coming up to rest on his muscular stomach. He was not opposed to having children; he liked kids. He liked their innocent curiosity, never-ending creativity, and general sweetness. When asked about his future, Mydei always pictured one with him living with his partner in a large, beautiful house with a spacious yard where their hypothetical children could run around and play to their little hearts’ content. “I want to keep it,” he whispered in a low voice. 

“Okay,” Hephaestion said simply, nodding slowly and smiling kindly at Mydei. “If that’s what you want, I’ll support you. No matter what.” Mydei felt a warmth enveloping him as he returned the smile

“Thank you, Hephaestion, that means a lot to me.” His shoulders relax, the invisible tension slowly melting away as he sinks into the comfortable booth. A beat of comfortable silence passed between them before Hephaestion broke it with the most important question. 

“So, who’s the father? Have you told him yet?” he asked curiously, eyes now bright as he leaned in. Mydei groaned.

“It’s Phainon. And yes, he already knows.” He’d be surprised if his friends still remembered the white haired man from their university years. So when Hephaestion suddenly sat up with his mouth slightly agape, Mydei became alarmed.

“Wait, Phainon? You mean the guy with white hair who followed you around like a lost puppy? The same one that you yelled at for burning the pasta in our Culinary Fundamentals class?” Mydei cringed at the memory. Phainon is still a total disaster in the kitchen. It's a miracle that he hasn’t burned down his apartment yet. “What did he say? Was he upset?”

“Yes, the same one,” he grumbled, slightly embarrassed. “I don’t know. I lied and said I was late for work and that we’ll discuss it later.” His best friend groaned in response.

“Oh Mydeimos, no! Why’d you leave the poor guy hanging like that?” he exclaimed with an exaggerated cry, hand pressed to his forehead in a display of mock despair. 

“Will you shut up? It’s not like I…” ran away from my problems. Again.

“As your best friend, it’s my duty to tell you that’s exactly what you’re doing,” Hephaestion replied seriously, his joking demeanor now having been replaced. “You can’t put this off or delay the inevitable with him. It’s not right for you, Phainon, or the baby. Don’t be an idiot.” Mydei hated to admit it, but Hephaestion was right. Tough but right. 

“Thank you, I think I needed to hear that,” Mydei admitted with a heavy sigh, feeling as if a giant weight had been lifted off his chest. “Don’t tell anyone about this. At least not right now, it’s still new and I don’t want to…” he trailed off, unable to finish his thought.

“Hey, don’t worry. Your ‘accidental lovechild with Phainon’ secret's safe with me.” Hephaestion beamed widely under Mydei’s thunderous glare. 

“I will murder you in your sleep if you utter that phrase to me again,” he threatened between gritted teeth. Still, Hephaestion just laughed, his usual jovial personality returning like nothing had happened. They eventually had to return to work as their customers lined up outside the shop, eager to buy their baked goods before they ran out. 

Mydei was more clear-headed and focused after his talk with Hephaestion; fewer mistakes were made, and he moved more comfortably around the kitchen. As the morning run began to slow down and they closed the shop for their afternoon break, Mydei fished his phone out of his apron pocket. 

He’s surprised to see a new message from Phainon and immediately opens it, his heart beating wildly in his chest.

I know you said we’ll talk about this later, but this is urgent. Can we meet tonight? There were none of the silly emojis Phainon usually used when he texts Mydei, which means that the other man is very serious. It made Mydei sweat and dread their imminent confrontation, but then he remembered Hephaestion’s words about facing the future. 

He cursed in Kremnoan before typing out his response, not bothering to read over it before hitting send. 

Phainon was now having a completely different crisis. He glared over at the perpetrator, his adoptive sister Cyrene who was innocently playing with Bubbles as if she hadn’t been the one to send Mydei that damned text. And now–

“Cyrene, why?!” he wailed before throwing himself onto the couch next to her, startling poor Bubbles, who gave his owner an unimpressed side eye. The pink-haired woman just snorted in amusement. 

“Gods, don’t be so dramatic, Phainon. You act like I just murdered the guy when all I did was give you two the push to talk about this,” Cyrene shrugged. he hated how right she was. He wished he could have done it alone, but it’s already too late. All he can do is wait. 

And wait, he does. Since he called the clinic to tell them that he’s going to have to take a day off for “personal issues,” all he could do now was pace around nervously and prepare himself for when Mydei comes to reject him. He took Bubbles out for his daily walk to try and clear his head when his phone finally chirped with a text notification. 

He almost dropped it while fishing it out of his pocket, his heart beating crazy hard in his chest as he finally managed to click on Mydei’s number and open their messages. 

Fine. I close tonight at 9. We can meet then, don’t be late. Phainon could cry with relief when he finished reading. Instead, he sent three thumbs-up emojis and got left on read almost immediately. He still smiled like an idiot. Bubbles remained unamused as he continued to munch on his neighbor's grass.

He had just ushered the last wave of customers out the door, Hephaestion left not long after them, but not before nagging Mydei not to stay up too late. He promised his friend half-heartedly and waved him goodnight. Now all alone with himself and Leo, the feline finally reappears from one of his many hiding spots. He scratches his pet under the chin before returning to clean. 

After mopping the floors, Mydei glances back up at the clock to see that he still has about an hour left before his and Phainon’s agreed-upon time. Feeling frustrated and agitated, Mydei heads back into the kitchen where he immediately starts to gather the ingredients for a tuskpir wrap. He’s always been a stress baker. Whenever he was too anxious or on edge, Mydei always found comfort in the kitchen. 

He made the sponge batter first before starting on the filling. The sweet scent of baking cake filled the air. Mydei was immediately taken back to his university years when he shared an apartment with Phainon.

He had been up all night trying to make the perfect dessert to make for his final presentation, testing different flavor combinations and using all his skill, just to be sorely disappointed at the end. Phainon, after learning to keep out of his way when Mydei got like that, bravely entered the kitchen to offer him some “inspiration”. 

Mydei had already ruled out having sex in the kitchen early in their transactional relationship (he thought it was downright disgusting to do it in a place where the food they ate was prepared). Still, the offer had been such a tempting escape from his stress that he caved almost immediately. He ended up passing the exam with high praise for his innovative version of a banana pie (he will never tell anyone about how he only came up with the idea when they were going down on each other). 

Sex with Phainon has always been great. He had always been a generous lover, making sure Mydei’s pleasure and comfort came first. He consistently asked for consent even when Mydei made the first move, he would never push Mydei’s hard limits, and would check in on him even in the middle of it. He was also a yapper, constantly praising Mydei by telling him how pretty and good he tasted, and how tight he felt around him. He’s obedient like a dog, actively listening and following through when Mydei tells him to be rougher, where to touch him. Phainon was also great with aftercare, ensuring Mydei stayed hydrated as he cleaned and hand-fed him snacks before they cuddled. 

Mydei couldn’t complain; he likes having Phainon around. While he had been reluctant at first, he now couldn’t imagine a more desirable, easy relationship. Except–

Sharp pain erupted from his hand, forcing him to drop the knife and look down at his bleeding finger. He had been so distracted when slicing the berries for the middle of the roll that he must have accidentally nicked the top of it. He put his injured finger into his mouth. The taste of blood and sweet fruit burst on his tongue, making him cringe before pulling his finger out to inspect the cut. Luckily, it wasn’t deep and the bleeding had almost stopped, but he still got the first aid kit to disinfect and bandage it. 

Mydei still didn’t stop, he washed the knife and cutting board before slicing up the rest of the fruit. After he finished that, Mydei moved on to the whipped cream filling. He kept his injured finger away from any pressure as he furiously whisked the cream, vanilla, and sugar together. He refrigerated both and waited for his timer to go off before carefully taking out the freshly baked roll. 

As always, the dessert came out perfectly light pink with the tuskpir’s signature darker pink swirls on top. Mydei was setting it out to cool when his mother texted him asking him two things: if he had gotten the package of Kremnoan history books yet, and if he’d be coming home for her birthday.

His stomach dropped at that last one. Mydei and his father never had a good relationship, and it had only gotten worse in recent years. His father had never liked how “soft” he was compared to the other children in their hometown or how his mother “constantly spoiled him”. In turn, Mydei hated his father for his cold, detached, and analytical views of the world. He was almost disowned after he got into a shouting match with his old man about not wanting to take over the family company and switched his studies to library sciences instead. 

“You don’t realize just how good you have it,” his father spat, his wrinkled grey face bright red. “Without our family, you’d have nothing. One day, you will see just how cruel and unforgiving the real world is.” 

They’ve barely spoken to each other since. His poor mother has done her best to try and mend their relationship, tried to get them in the same room and at least share a drink, but it never worked. Mydei felt guilty, solely because he knew how much it hurt her, but the damage had been done, and he was perfectly content with his new life far away from his old man. He typed out the first message and thanked her for the books before giving her a vague, half-hearted excuse about checking his schedule. 

In truth, he missed her so much. He missed her warm hugs, her beautiful smile, and her asking him about his day as they shared a glass of wine. He wished he could go back home as often as she’d like, but that would mean seeing his father too. Despite not looking the part, Mydei’s father is very good to her, obviously still cherishing and loving her every day. If only he were like that with the very child he created.

Mydei snorted sarcastically before layering on the cream and berries onto the roll. Once the filling was all used up, he began to close up his dessert with his rolling pin. After making sure it’s sealed shut properly, Mydei took a step back to admire his hard work before moving it onto a clean plate. He looked over at the clock to see that it was already almost time for them to meet. He wiped his hands off on his apron and took the cake wrap back out to the cafe’s cozy dining area. 

Leo perked up from his spot in one of the chairs and immediately trotted over, jumping up onto the table to curiously sniff at the pink dessert. “Hey, not for you,” Mydei lightly scolded before picking him up and depositing him back on the floor. The stubborn cat let out a truly pitiful meow and reached up on his hind legs to try and bat at his hand again, only for Mydei to gently push him back down. “Go away. I already fed you, this stuff isn’t good for cats.” 

He picked up Leo and was about to take him upstairs to his apartment when the store chime went off as someone opened the door. “Sorry, we’re closed for the night,” Mydei started to explain out of habit before looking up to see an amused yet slightly confused Phainon. “Oh, it’s just you. You’re early.”

“Well, you told me not to be late,” the other man chuckled back awkwardly. He’s dressed in a rather awful color combination, a plain orange tee and baggy green gym shorts. Like an upside-down pumpkin, Mydei couldn’t help but think to himself as he bit the inside of his cheek to keep from laughing. It’s so off-putting that he didn’t notice the fact that Phainon was holding a takeout bag from Mydei’s favorite place.

The smell of the oily fast food assaulted his nose. His mouth began to water after realizing how long it’s been since his last full meal. “I figured I’d bring some dinner over since I know how you get, staying past closing to keep baking,” Phainon explained before placing the greasy paper bag on the table next to their dessert and taking a seat. Mydei, who was too hungry to be annoyed about having to clean up the grease, just placed Leo back on the floor. He sat across from the other man before Phainon handed him his bowl of fried rice along with a spring roll. 

The rambunctious feline beelineed for Phainon, meowing incessantly to be pet and fed small scraps of their dinner. Phainon indulged, smiling when Mydei’s cat jumped up into his lap, stroking Leo’s soft ginger fur as the animal curled up and took a nap. Mydei snorted and pretended not to be hurt over the favoritism. 

They ate in familiar silence, although Mydei could feel Phainon’s heavy stare boring into him. The fried rice was good, but not as good as he remembered. Mydei still forced himself to finish the bowl, cringing at the uncomfortable film of oil on his tongue. He offered his spring roll to Phainon, who took it without a question, a knowing gleam in his bright blue eyes. 

“So…” Phainon finally started, his eyes drifting down to Mydei’s midsection with a careful expression. Mydei can’t help but curl an arm around it in a protective manner. “We should talk about the…um…” he stammered, scratching the back of his head with an awkward motion. 

“Baby,” Mydei finished for him, arm tightening around his stomach. 

“Yes, right. The baby we uh…” Phainon cleared his throat, disturbing Leo from his lap and causing him to saunter off with an unamused glance. “Are you going to–”

“I’m keeping it,” Mydei interrupted before the sentence could be finished, finally looking away to look down at where the baby should be growing. He balled up his apron in his fists and waited. The silence that followed felt like an eternity, but Mydei couldn't bring himself to look up and see Phainon’s expression. 

Would he be angry, furious, and demand that Mydei get an abortion anyway? No, he couldn’t picture a man who is usually so kind, thoughtful, and gentle saying something so cruel like that to him. Mydei finally gathered the courage to look up and see Phainon’s patient smile, the sight of it made his shoulders relax. 

“Okay,” he replied in a soft voice. Mydei uncrossed his arms. He’s surprised by what Phainon said next. “As long as that’s your real answer, I’m happy. I wanted to keep it too.”

“Really?” Mydei couldn’t help but ask, his heart skipping a beat. “Are you sure, you’re not just saying that, right?” he narrowed his eyes in suspicion, which caused Phainon to immediately shake his head. 

“No, I mean it! I remember you saying how much you wanted kids when we were still and school, and I’ve always wanted them with–” he stopped his sentence abruptly, his eyes wide before he pretended to cough into his fist. “I mean, I feel the same way about kids. Wanting my own, I mean.”

Strange. Mydei wanted to ask more, but didn’t want to press on in case it upset Phainon. “Alright, since we’re both wanting to keep the baby, we should probably lay down some ground rules.” Phainon groaned melodramatically at that which he ignored. 

“More rules, seriously, Mydei? I already had trouble keeping up with them when we were still in school,” Phainon whined, his expression melting into one akin to a kicked puppy dog. Mydei, unsympathetic to his plight, just snorted in amusement. 

“That’s more of a ‘you’ problem,” he retorted with a smirk, his body relaxing further into the seat as they fell back into their usual banter. “They’re not rules, just some sort of agreement set in place before the baby comes.”

“What sort of agreement?” Phainon inquired. 

“I suppose how involved you would like to be in the future with the baby. Do we move into a new place together, or would you like to keep–”

“I think that’d be the best option,” Phainon interrupted again, much quicker than before. Mydei arched an eyebrow in surprise. “I mean, it’ll be like we’re in school again. I already know your schedule and you know mine, so it shouldn’t be too difficult for us to get along.” That does make sense, so Mydei doesn’t comment on his outburst. 

“Alright, if you’re amicable to it. I have no objections,” he shrugged, not noticing the excited, victorious gleam in Phainon’s cerulean eyes. “What about telling our parents? I’m sure yours will be ecstatic about the news.” Mydei tried not to sound too bitter about it. He knew his mother would be over the moon, but his father–

Let’s just say he’d have some choice words that should not be said around anyone. “We can wait on telling them and everyone else.
