Have you been taking care of yourself? Are you getting enough sleep?” she interrogates, causing Phainon to smile slightly. 

“Been trying to,” he replies honestly. He then hears the patio door slide open as his father steps back inside after working in their garden. He smiles as he listens to his parents’ affectionate cooing as Hierynomus offers Audata the freshly cut roses from their rose bush. After Phainon moved out for college, his parents suffered a severe case of empty nest syndrome since he was their only child. They tried many new activities to keep themselves busy, like painting, cooking, and knitting, until they discovered how much fun gardening was. 

By the time Phainon returned for the holiday break, their spacious backyard had practically been converted into a mini botanical garden with various flowers, vegetables, and fruit. It was a labor of love that has most certainly paid off, bringing his parents closer together in his absence.. 

“Is that you, son?” Hierynomus takes over the call as Phainon’s mother goes to put the flowers in water. “It’s been a while, how’s work?” 

“It’s alright, busy as usual,” Phainon replies. “How’s the harvest going?” His father lets out a small sigh. 

“Something’s been getting into the tomatoes at night, so I’ve been laying out traps to try and catch it. I think it’s a raccoon, but your mother thinks it’s just the neighbor’s cat.” Phainon chuckles, listening to the mundane happenings back at home makes the invisible weight off his shoulders lift.  

“Well, you have to send me a picture of the criminal once you catch them, alright?” he jokes back, Hierynomus copies. 

“Of course. Anyway, is there something else you wanted to talk about? How’s Bubbles? Have you talked to Cyrene recently? How is she? What about…um, Mydei, was it? How is he?” Phainon’s parents met Mydei a few times before when they shared an apartment in school, but Phainon has never told them about their special “relationship” (because why would he?). As the realization dawns on him that he has to be the one to break the news, a pit forms in Phainon’s stomach. 

“They’re fine. Cyrene is watching Bubbles for me. Mydei…uh, actually, there’s something I need to tell both you and Mom. Is she still there?” He tries not to panic as he hears his father call her over, the tension in the air suddenly becoming more palpable. 

“Phainon, what’s wrong? Did something happen?” Audata asks, her voice soft and worried. 

“You can tell us anything, son. We won’t be mad,” Hierynomus adds helpfully. 

“I know,” Phainon speaks softly before taking a deep breath. “Mydei and I are expecting a baby. He’s pregnant.” The silence that follows is nerve-wracking. Phainon tries not to sweat through his work scrubs as he nervously waits for their reaction. They wouldn’t force him to break contact with Mydei, right? 

“Phainon,” his father starts, his voice slightly trembling. He braces himself for the fallout, already beginning to prepare for his defense just in case. That’s fantastic news! We weren’t even aware that you two were seeing each other.” Phainon bites his lip; the guilt building up inside him makes him feel ill. He briefly entertains the idea of agreeing, but realizes how much of a mess that would be if the truth came out. 

“We’re not,” he mumbles begrudgingly. He wants the ground to swallow him so he wouldn’t have to experience the awkward, tense silence that followed right after. Nonetheless, he forces himself to keep going. “It wasn’t planned at first, but we’ve come to a mutual agreement. I told Mydei I want to be as involved as possible for him and the baby.” 

“Do his parents know yet?” Phainon quickly tells them no. Mydei hasn’t reached out to his side of the family yet (no doubt avoiding his father). “I see,” Audata replies calmly. “How far along is he?” 

“About twelve weeks now, the doctor said it was safe to start telling people,” he answers dutifully. 

“And the two of you are sure this is something you want to go through with?” Hierynomus catechizes, stern but not unhappy. Phainon swallows, steeling his resolve and answers.

“Yes,” his voice doesn’t shake, doesn’t falter. He’s certain, one hundred percent. “I’ve never been more certain about anything.” There’s another pause before Audata whispers something, but it’s too quiet and fast for Phainon to interpret clearly. His father hums in response before murmuring back.

“If it’s what you two have agreed upon, then we trust and support your decision on this. Wholeheartedly.” Phainon is so relieved that he could almost cry. 

“Thanks. For a second, I thought you guys would be pissed about us suddenly making you grandparents,” he jokes awkwardly while cringing inwardly. Mydei and Cyrene have mentioned that he does have a habit of putting his foot in his mouth in tense situations. But he’ll count that as a win when he hears his father let out a chuckle. 

“You’re a grown man, Phainon. You have your own life now, and we can’t control everything you do, only offer advice and help when you need it,” his mother says. “No matter what happens, just remember that we’ll always be here for you and that we love you very much.” 

He blinks back the harsh sting of tears that suddenly emerge in his eyes. “I know. I love both of you, too.”   

“Why don’t you bring Mydei home for dinner one night? I’m sure he’ll appreciate a good home-cooked meal that he doesn’t have to prepare himself or worry about you accidentally burning his kitchen to the ground. No offense, son.” 

Phainon lets out a laugh, a real one this time. “Offense taken, old man. But sure, that sounds like a great idea. I’ll ask him later tonight. But I have to get back to work now, so I’ll talk to you later?”

“Of course, please take care of yourself, Phainon.” They remind him before finally wrapping their goodbyes and hanging up. He goes back inside feeling a thousand times lighter.

“Your parents want to meet me? Haven’t they already?” Mydei asks Phainon who’s sitting at the counter bar, munching on the pastry Mydei forced onto him (another old habit from school, Phainon had always been willing to be his test-subject-slash-guinea-pig whenever it came to Mydei’s wackier recipes. This time, it was an apple pie mixed with a handful of shredded cheddar cheese). 

Phainon scraps up the last of the pie crust with his fork before answering, “They just want to get to know you better since you’re carrying…our baby.” He hesitated briefly. Mydei frowns, still not convinced. 

“You sure that’s a good idea? They’re not too upset about their first grandchild being a bastard?” The word sounds harsh, it hurts Mydei to have to say it aloud, but it is true. He misses the way Phainon visibly perks up at that.  

“If it bothers you that much, you know we can have a quick ceremony,” he suggests eagerly, his cerulean blue eyes sparkling brightly. Mydei scoffs at that before returning to wiping down the countertop, his face feels strangely warm at the thought. 

“Idiot, that’s not what I’m talking about. I’m asking you, how are you so sure they’re honestly okay with our…situation? What if they feel like I’m just a burden and a dead weight holding back their precious ‘golden boy’?” He hadn’t meant for it to come out so harshly, but the thought suddenly occurred to him. 

Was that all he would be in the future, a weight that holds Phainon back from achieving the life he deserved? Anchoring him down to a heated night of misplaced passion? The thought makes Mydei sick; he could almost feel the bile rising up the back of his throat. He furiously scrubs at a stubborn coffee stain, all of his anger and frustration channeled into that one spot, until Phainon suddenly reaches out to gently place his hand over Mydei’s.

He finally looks up to stare back into those saddened blue eyes and that handsome face twisted into a sad frown. Even the antenna hairs at the top of his head seemed to have deflated (how was that even possible? Hair doesn’t do that, does it?). “Is that what you really think about yourself and our baby?”

You’ve been nothing but a disappointment to me. How do you think you’ll be able to carry on our family name if you continue like this? The mini version of his father scoffs in his head. Mydei grits his teeth, pulling away from Phainon. 

Shut the fuck up, he growls back. You know nothing about me, old man. And you never will.  

“I’m just offering you an out here. If you ever want to back out, do it before it gets too serious or before other people get involved,” he diverts coolly, about to walk back into the kitchen, when Phainon grabs his wrist. 

“How many more times do I have to tell you that I’m very serious about this, Mydeimos?” he snaps back, his voice cold and stern. It’s rare when he loses his temper with Mydei, and it’s even rarer when he uses his full name. Mydei realizes that must have genuinely pissed Phainon off. He doesn’t break free from his grip; Phainon’s hold is too strong. 

“I’m just saying—”

“Stop listening to those voices, Mydei, and listen to me,” Phainon interrupts (that’s another rarity). “I don’t want to be anywhere else that isn’t here with you. Nothing will change that. Not my parents, not our friends. Hell, not even if my supposed soulmate walked through that door right now. I’m staying, and the only way you’re getting rid of me is burying me at my funeral.” 

Mydei is speechless; he has always known Phainon was the more emotional of the two between them. He’s seen him cry over movies where the dog dies, when Bubbles faked being sick that one time to try and get his sandwich, and when Cyrene had to go back to school. He’s seen Phainon's passion for helping people get better and comforting them when they got frustrated. But he’s never been the reason for this sort of passion. 

It’s strange. It makes Mydei’s heart beat faster and causes his whole body to heat up. He realizes that he doesn’t hate it—he likes it. He wants to see it more and be in its presence when it happens again. 

“Mydei, are you okay?” Phainon’s concerned voice suddenly breaks through the strange fog overtaking his tired-addled brain. He stutters, “I’m sorry! I didn’t mean to scare you like that; it just came out.” His panic only grew when Mydei didn’t reply. “Please, say something. I’m sorry.” The loosening grip on his arm jerks Mydei back into action. 

“I’m fine,” he stutters out before clearing his throat. “You didn’t scare me. I just…wasn’t expecting that.” Phainon deflates even more, his shoulders fall. The sight is so pitiful that Mydei can’t help but chuckle a little. He really is like a little puppy, Mydei muses to himself. “I’m not saying it was bad. In fact, it was somewhat reassuring to listen to. Thank you, Phainon.” Right on cue, the man perks up again. Mydei did not doubt that if he had a tail, it would be wagging furiously. “So, when did your parents say we can come over for dinner? I’m curious to see where you got your terrible cooking skills from.” 

Before Phainon could protest or defend himself, the store door chime rang, startling them out of their little bubble. Standing at the entrance are Leonnius and Plolemy, having finished wrangling Leo back up to Mydei’s apartment. If looks could kill, Phainon would be twelve feet under (six feet for each). 

“Sorry, are we interrupting anything? What are you doing here?” Ptolemy practically snarls at Phainon, who winces but doesn’t let go of Mydei. Leonnius just silently glares at him (he’s still a little salty that Hephaestion didn’t tell him the truth when they stopped by to check up on him) until Mydei intervenes.

“Lemy, Leon, it’s fine. Phainon and I were just talking.” Mydei finally extracts himself from his hold and walks over to his friends. “Why don’t you guys head home for the night? I really appreciate the two of you helping out at the cafe today. I’ll lock up.” He gently ushers them out the door, not missing the dirty looks they still flash over their shoulders as they leave. 

Phainon lets out a heavy sigh of relief when Mydei locks the door behind them. “I’m guessing they don’t really like me?” he asks rhetorically. Mydei laughs and shakes his head. 

“No, you’re not their favorite person right now,” he chuckles while Phainon groans. 

“I told you I should have written out a will beforehand. If you hear about my death in the news, just know it was most likely Peucesta.”

Mydei tries not to fiddle with the bouquet in his hands as Phainon reaches out to ring his parents’ doorbell. Phainon puts a reassuring hand on his shoulder and gently squeezes it. “Don’t be so nervous, they’re going to love you.” 

How would you know that ? Mydei retorts in his head, he’s about to say it aloud when he hears the footsteps getting closer. Oh Gods, he shouldn’t have agreed to this. Would it be considered rude if he told them he wasn’t feeling well (not a total lie, he’s been feeling pretty nauseous lately)? What if the flowers he chose at the store had another meaning in Aedes Elysiae? He should have gone with his gut and gotten the other bouquet as a backup. He turns to Phainon, about to cough up some flimsy excuse, when the door swings open and floods the porch in warm yellow light. 

“Phainon! And Mydei, you’ve arrived! Just in time, too, your father is putting the lamb in the oven. Please come in, you two!” Audata smiles cheerfully before ushering them inside. Phainon has her smile and bright blue eyes, which beautifully complement her silvery pale hair, plaited artfully to rest over her shoulder. 

Phainon gently pushes Mydei over the threshold with his hand on the small of his back, making him stumble inside. He tries to shoot him a fierce glare, but Phainon doesn’t notice as he bends down to kiss his mother on the cheek. “How are you, sweetheart? I hope the drive down here wasn’t too bad,” she says as Phainon takes off his shoes. Mydei follows suit. 

“Eh, there was some traffic, but then it cleared as soon as we got out of the city,” Phainon replies, his hand never leaving Mydei’s back as he draws him close to his side. “You still remember Mydeimos, right?” Her kindness doesn’t falter as her gaze flickers over to Mydei, her eyes softening as she looks him over.

“Of course I do. How are you feeling, dear? Not too horribly, I hope. I still remember having terrible morning sickness when I was pregnant with Phainon. I hope he’s been taking care of you properly; otherwise, I’d have to give him another stern talking.” 

“Mom, please,” Phainon groans. Mydei chuckles and tries to hide it behind a cough when he turns to glare at Mydei in betrayal. 

“Don’t worry, ma’am, he’s been on his best behavior, I just have a little bit of nausea here and there," he admits nervously before holding out the daisies for her to take. “But he told me how much you and your husband enjoy gardening, so I got you these. I hope you like them.” Audata’s eyes widen in appreciation before gingerly taking them from Mydei. 

“Oh, how lovely! Thank you, Mydeimos, they’re beautiful,” she gushes as she presses them up to her nose, taking in their sweet perfume. She then takes his hand, gently tugging him deeper into their home. “Let me put these in some water first, and then I’ll give you a tour. I’ll even show you Phainon’s old room. You know, as a little boy, he was a big fan of the Chrysos Heirs. He would always beg us for the latest action figure or the newest print and plaster them on his wall. We haven’t touched his room since he left, so why don’t we–”

“Mom!” Phainon squawks, his face now a brilliant shade of red. He fumes as both Mydei and Audata double over with amused giggles. “Whatever, if you’re just going to laugh at me, I’m going to help Dad,” he huffs before storming off, finally leaving Mydei’s side. Audata finally manages to stop laughing and smiles over at Mydei. 

“I’m sorry, it’s just so much fun to rile him up like that,” she admits. 

“I know,” Mydei agrees, “I used to do the same thing back in college when he wouldn’t leave me alone.” He shakes his head. 

“Such a silly boy. Here, why don’t you take a seat out in the garden, and I’ll join you shortly?” Audata kindly leads him through the living room, past their impressive-looking kitchen, where Phainon is chatting with his father. Hierynomus looks up to briefly smile at Mydei. Phainon is a spitting image of the man, all the way to the matching ahoge that stand at the top of his head, down to their similar body builds.  

Audata leads him towards their backyard, and he’s instantly impressed by the greenery and flowers growing there. The flowers are aromatic and sweet, their scent wafts around like a pleasant perfume. Audata helpfully points out all the items in the garden as Mydei dutifully listens until she finally ducks back inside to check in on their dinner, leaving him alone to explore on his own. 

As he reaches out to gently caress the petals of the rosebush, he tries to picture what his future would be like after their baby arrives. 

Mydei smiled as his child came running back with the rose in their chubby little hand. “Mama, pretty flower!” they shouted in excitement before Mydei scooped them up into his arms. They had Phainon’s eyes and Mydei’s blond hair. He kissed their soft cheeks until they giggled and pushed his face away. “For Mama!” they repeated and pressed the rose into Mydei’s face. He took it from them before it could be stabbed into his eye. 

“It’s beautiful. Thank you, my little bean,” he replied, squeezing them in his arms as they affectionately nuzzle against his neck.  He heard that familiar chuckle before those same arms wrapped around them, Phainon’s firm chest pressed up against Mydei’s back. He felt the other man’s lip graze the side of his head, a gentle and sweet gesture. 

“Papa!” their baby squealed in excitement. Phainon laughed and gently tussled their soft, downy beige hair. Mydei sighed before leaning into Phainon’s body; he felt content and safe. It’s wonderful

“Mydei, are you alright? You’ve been staring at the same rose shrub for a while now,” Phainon comes up behind him, startling Mydei out of his imagination while holding a tall glass of juice in his hand. 

“I’m fine,” he replies hoarsely, clearing his throat before continuing. “Just a little tired.” Mydei takes the glass from him and takes a sip. To his surprise, it’s his favorite, pomegranate juice with a splash of milk and honey. He even managed to get the proper ratios, so it wasn’t too sweet or watered down. It’s perfect. 

“Mom and Dad said the food should be out soon,” Phainon reports before stepping to Mydei’s side, marveling at the same flower Mydei was studying before reaching out and plucking it straight off the bush.

“Phainon–” he tries to scold him when Phainon wordlessly offers it to Mydei. 

“Take it, it’s fine. My parents won’t miss it. Besides, these types of roses grow back pretty fast,” he reassures Mydei, gently pushing the flower into Mydei’s hand. The stem is spineless and smooth, thick and healthy, with beautifully pastel pink petals. It has a slight fruity perfume with a lemony note. It’s quite pleasant. “It’s one of my favorite flowers in the whole garden.”

“Thank you, it’s lovely,” he says as he cradles the delicate bud. Phainon smiles widely before leading him back to the patio where the fire pit has been lit, bathing the area in warm orange light. Hierynomus and Audata are waiting for them at the dining table, smiling before inviting them to sit down, their dinner already ready for them.

Dinner goes well, the food is fantastic (the best Mydei’s ever had, how did Phainon not inherit any of that talent?), and the conversation is easy. Hierynomus and Audata make sure not to discuss anything that makes Mydei uncomfortable, instead sticking to general topics like his job, his hobbies, and his favorite pastries to make for the cafe. He’s almost forgotten the reason he was invited over in the first place until they slip up and ask about Mydei’s parents.

“So, will you be telling your mother and father about the pregnancy as well?” Hierynomus asks innocently. Phainon stiffens by his side, as Mydei tries not to choke. Audata seems to have sensed their unease because she lightly slaps her husband’s arm. Hierynomus appears to have realized his mistakes and instantly tries to apologize.  

“It’s alright,” Mydei reassures after a beat of silence. “I’ll tell her. Eventually,” he says, purposefully leaving out his father. His stomach twists unpleasantly as he tries not to think about having to tell his father the news. Phainon coughs, the silence that falls over them is awkward and stifling until Audata finally stands up and asks Mydei for his help to get the dessert. 

Grateful for the distraction, Mydei gets up and follows her inside. Their dessert is a decadent-looking three-tiered chocolate and raspberry cake—Mydei’s mouth waters just from looking at it. “It looks delicious,” Mydei compliments. Audata cuts out a large piece and puts it on his plate, almost like she already knew. Audata reaches out to put extra raspberries to garnish on their slices before leaning back with a serious gleam in her eyes. 

She giggles when he flushes in embarrassment, “This is one of Phainon’s favorites, but I had a feeling you’d like this as well,” she explains before cutting out more pieces for the rest of them. “But I also wanted to take a moment to talk to you alone, without Phainon or my husband hearing us.” 

She turns to face Mydei with a sad but understanding voice, “Phainon mentioned to us your relationship with your…father. There wasn’t a lot of detail to go off of, but is it correct to assume that the two of you don’t get along?” Mydei sighs. 

“That’s the nicest way of putting it,” he admits with his arms crossed over his chest. “He was always really tough on me, expected me to follow in his footsteps and inherit the family business. I never wanted to, so when I went to college, we hardly spoke to each other. When I was in school, I changed my major, and we got into a huge fight over it. I haven’t called him since.” Mydei looks down at his feet, the bitterness of the memory is raw on his tongue.  

“Ah, I see,” Audata says softly after a moment of solemn silence. “So you’re afraid he won’t take the news about the baby well,” she asks rhetorically. Mydei can’t help but snort. 

“I know he won’t take it well, he’s always been a traditionalist, conservative,” he laughs humorlessly before apologizing. “I know it’s not funny. It’s just–”

“I know, I understand. You don’t have to explain your pain to me, Mydeimos,” she comforts him kindly. It reminds him so much of his own mother that it makes tears well up in his eyes. “Just…if you ever need anything, or have any questions, please ask me. I can give you my number before you leave so you can call me whenever. I will be more than happy to come up to the city and help with anything.” 

“I–thank you,” he mutters sincerely. Aedes Elysiae is a little closer to Okhema than Castrum Kremnos, so hopefully it wouldn’t be too much trouble for Audata to come up and visit before the baby came.   

He follows her back out to see Phainon and his father deep in conversation, Phainon’s brows furrowed together in thought. He seems troubled, like he’s trying to solve a complicated math problem (Mydei can’t relate; he’s always been terrible at math). Still, when he sees Mydei coming back, his befuddled expression melts away and back into his usual bright sunny smile. 

He thanks Mydei as he hands him his portion, his eyes lighting up in excitement as he starts to dig in. It’s a surprisingly cute sight to see a grown man be so happy to eat a chocolate cake. Mydei takes a bite and can understand why it’s one of Phainon’s favorites. It’s rich, sweet, but not too sweet, with a layer of raspberry jelly and chocolate ganache. 

Mydei can’t remember the last time someone cooked for him, took care of him like this. His heart aches, but at the same time softens. He catches Audata’s soft gaze from across the table as she smiles at Phainon. It’s a motherly gaze, full of love and happiness now that her son is back home. One day, Mydei will get to experience that joy, that same fierce love only a mother could have for their child. He places his hand on his stomach, a small smile tickles the side of his lips.

He can’t wait for his turn.

chapters.title: Chapter 5
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

The fated reunion with Mydei's parents. TW: Mydei's dad. Again.

Chapter Notes

Yay, a super loooong chapter, sorry about the wait! I initially wanted to make it two chapters, but it didn't feel right to drag it out, so there you have it!

Anyway, can you tell how much I hate Mydei's dad? Honestly, fuck that guy. Please enjoy anyway, I tried to make it as sweet as possible near the end <3

Phainon is jolted out of bed by the sound of loud clattering coming from the kitchen. Bubbles, who, after a long day of trying to win over the cat’s affections, sprang up from his deep sleep and started whining. Phainon shushes the dog with a few ear scratches before reaching over to Mydei’s side of the bed, only to find it cold and empty. He blinks and reaches for his phone to check the time, his eyes widen when he finally manages to blink away the rest of the sleep from his eyes. 

He gets out of bed and tiptoes over to the kitchen, where he sees the baker in just his pajama pants, chopping up vegetables. “Mydei, what are you doing?” Mydei jumps, startled from his task of making a late-night snack, to see Phainon standing in the doorway with a curious tilt of his head. 

“Gods, you scared me. I was hungry and couldn’t sleep, so I thought I’d try some of these instant noodles.” Mydei states bluntly before opening the package and dumping the noodles into the boiling water. Phainon (ignoring the rule of never going into the kitchen) walks over to his side and reads the label.

“Spicy beef offal stew ramen, with extra hot chili oil sauce? I thought you didn’t like spicy foods,” Phainon reads aloud. Mydei coughs.

“I don’t, it's just...the baby wants it,” he admits with a reluctant mumble, his face turning a lovely shade of pink. Phainon does his best to hide his amused snort with a cough. Mydei is so cute. Phainon’s eyes drift down to Mydei’s slightly protruding stomach, warmth filling Phainon’s chest as he thinks about their baby growing inside of him. 

He just started showing not long after they visited Phainon’s parents, storming into their shared bedroom one night with his hands clutching his middle and demanding that Phainon see and feel for himself. When he noticed it, Phainon broke down into happy tears. Mydei just laughed and teased him for being a big crybaby, but Phainon knew he had been crying too. 

Now, every day with Mydei’s permission, Phainon gets to touch their little bump–their baby. And each day, Phainon falls more and more in love with them and Mydei. 

“I should be asking you that question, though. It’s almost three in the morning. What are you doing up this late?”

“I heard a loud noise and just came in to see what was going on,” Phainon explains, just as Mydei goes to pick up the knife to continue cutting up the vegetables. “Wait, let me do it, Mydei.” He reaches out, only for Mydei to pull away. 

“You know you don’t have to do everything your mother tells you to do, Phainon,” Mydei snorts sarcastically. “I’m still capable of doing things on my own.” 

“But I want to,” Phainon pouts, his blue eyes round and shiny as he stares back at Mydei. He knows how strong Mydei is, how capable and intelligent he has always been. He’s already handled all his bodily changes like a champ so far, despite complaining about how tired and sore he feels after work. Phainon wants to help alleviate some of that pressure in whatever way he can. “Please, Mydei. I promise I won’t burn down the kitchen this time.” (he tries not to think back to the time he accidentally burnt the toast and set off the sprinklers in the apartment one time, causing their entire complex to be evacuated.)

Mydei sighs and, much to Phainon’s surprise, allows him to take the knife and moves the cutting board towards him. “Fine. Just try not to butcher the rest of the vegetables or cut your fingers off,” he warns as Phainon excitedly takes over. His knife skills are, of course, not as professional or neat like Mydei’s, but he does his best to try and cut them down to the same size. Mydei doesn’t comment on the mismatching portions as Phainon gently tosses the leafy greens into the pot with the cooking noodles. 

Mydei is even quieter than usual; something must be bothering him. Usually, he would get annoyed with Phainon for trying to take over or for being overly protective of him. They’ll argue back and forth for a little bit before one of them gives in (Mydei was winning by only a few), but recently he’s been more…distracted. When Phainon goes to pour in the seasoning packet and the chili oil, Mydei instructs him to pour out the entire thing. The soup turns a bright, spicy red color that makes Phainon’s stomach turn, but if it’s what Mydei wants, he’ll do it. 

Mydei doesn’t even complain when Phainon carries the now heavy pot, now full of instant noodles and spicy soup, out into the dining area. He quietly watches Mydei, his golden eyes are bright as he eagerly begins to devour the noodles and slurps up the soup. Phainon continues to just watch on in amusement, his elbow resting on the table with his palm propping up his face. 

“You can go back to bed if you want. It’s late, you don’t have to stay up with me,” Mydei informs him in between bites, but Phaion shakes his head.

“It’s fine, I don’t mind,” Phainon replies with a big smile while fighting back the urge to yawn. Mydei narrows his eyes but goes back to eating until the pot is spotless. Once he’s finished, Mydei leans back in his chair with a deep sigh and closes his eyes. But instead of looking content and relaxed after a meal, his brows are furrowed in frustration.  Phainon, after hesitating for a moment, finally asks.

“Is everything okay with you, Mydei? You’ve been awfully quiet lately. Is it the baby? Are you in pain? Should we call the hospital?” he nervously lists, his eyes darting between the growing baby bump and Mydei’s face.

“No, it’s not that,” Mydei hesitates for a moment before reluctantly continuing. “It’s my mother. Her birthday is coming up soon, and she’s invited me back home for a dinner party to celebrate.” It should be good news, Phainon knows how much he adores his mothers, still remembering their long conversations when Mydei was still in school, and how they’d talk for hours. 

It should be considered as a sweet gesture that she wants him to be there for her birthday, but by studying the conflicted expression on Mydei’s face, the situation is much more complicated than that. 

“You don’t want to see your dad while you’re there,” Phainon correctly hypothesizes, the defeated groan from his is the only response Phainon gets. “And they still don’t know about the baby.” 

“No, they don’t,” Mydei admits, his hand resting on top of the bump. “I want to tell her before it becomes too noticeable. My father…it’ll be impossible for him not to know, especially after I tell my mother.” Phainon feels a strong pang of sympathy. 

“So, when are you going to finally break the news to them?” he asks curiously. 

“Preferably after her birthday, that way I’ll have more time to prepare what I want to say and it won’t take anything away leading up to her special day,” Mydei explains while caressing his abdomen, his eyes softening as he stares down at the baby. Phainon’s heart softens at the sight, his love for Mydei only deepening with each breath. 

Mydei lets out another deep, exasperated groan as he digs the heels of his hands into his eyes. “I should have told her that I have something that night, then I wouldn’t even have to go.” Phainon perks up at that.

“You’re going on your own? What about Hephaestion and everyone else?” he inquires. 

“They weren’t invited, it’s mostly just going to be my parents, Krateros, and a few of their close friends and colleagues,” Mydei replied, and moved his hands away from his eyes. They get up to clean. Phainon washes the pot and utensils in the sink while Mydei wipes down the dining table, still ranting to Phainon over the sound of water running. 

“They’re going to ask all these weird, invasive questions, force me to interact with my father, and—ugh, maybe I should have just told her no, that I don’t know anyone else that’s going to be there.” Phainon finishes rinsing off the pot when he comes up with an idea. He strolls back into the dining room. 

“Then, why don’t I come with you?” he offers blatantly. Mydei chokes.

“What, are you serious?” He nods determinedly. “Phainon, you never even met my parents.” The white haired man shrugs nonchalantly. 

“I’ve lived with you throughout our college career, I think I’ve got a pretty good basis on what they’re like through your phone calls and interactions.” Mydei clenches his jaw.

“What if they don’t like you?” Phainon shrugs his shoulders again. 

“I know plenty of people who already don’t like me! Remember that one really pretentious girl and her group of friends in our Philosophy class, Caenis or whatever? She hated my guts.” Phainon retold. Mydei rolls his eyes. 

“Wow, one of our classmates back in school disliked it every time you spoke in class, a real shocker,” he snorts. “We’re not talking about the same type of people here, Phainon. My father attracts a specific type of…businessmen. They’re not the type of people who associate with people like you.” 

Ouch. 

“Ouch,” Phainon comments in a half-joking way. He knows that he and his family are not among the super wealthy, but they make enough to live a relatively comfortable life. Mydei must have sensed that he stepped on a nerve because he winces slightly. 

“That’s not what I meant. Phainon, it’s just that these people aren’t particularly kind to outsiders; they look down on those they deem inferior. It’s a class thing that my father unfortunately falls victim to. I don’t want to put you in any uncomfortable positions like that if you do end up coming with me, I’d rather be the only one who handles all their ridicule,” Mydei admits, his shoulders sagging with defeat. Phainon doesn’t hesitate to take his hand and gives it a reassuring squeeze. 

“I know, but you don’t have to do it on your own. Remember when I told you that I never wanted you to feel like you’re all alone in this? It wasn’t meant for just the pregnancy and the baby. For whatever it is that you need, I’ll be there.” 

For a moment, Mydei just stares at him with a curious expression. His brows are furrowed in concentration, golden eyes shining brightly as they study Phainon from head to toe. Finally, after what felt like an eternity, Mydei complies. 

“Fine, I’ll call my mother tomorrow about bringing a plus one. We have two weeks until the party to prepare for. Wear something nice because if I catch you wearing that horrible chimera print tie, I’m throwing it into a fire.” Phainon’s smile is so wide he’s almost afraid that his face will split apart. 

“Don’t worry, it’s all going to be okay, I promise. It’s a date then, Mydeimos.”

Mydei should have realized sooner that the night was going to be a disaster the second they stepped out of the car and stared up at the grand mansion that he grew up in. Phainon, with his wild pale bangs slicked back and dressed in a nicely tailored all-black suit (Mydei had taken them out shopping a few days prior), openly gawks as they climb up the stairs to the main entrance. 

He can’t help but snort at the other’s bewildered expression. “I know you said your family was rich, but you never mentioned that they were this kind of rich,” Phainon expounds lamely. Mydei snorts. 

“What’d you expect? I did mention that my father is in charge of one of Castrum Kremnos’s largest financing businesses.” He taps Phainon on the chin. “Make sure to close your mouth before you go in, or else you want everyone there to think you’re some slackjaw clown that wandered in from the outside.” 

Phainon does as he’s told and sticks close to Mydei’s side, never wandering far as they walk up to the door. Mydei rings the doorbell (even though it’s his home) and greets the wait staff his father hired for the night. He can see the majority of the party already mingling around, the party already in swing. Some glance over at him before scandalously whispering behind secretive hands, but Mydei pays them no mind. 

The other sign of the impending catastrophe was that when the two finally stepped inside, they were immediately offered two tall flutes of bubbly champagne. Mydei takes one just to be polite and to avoid suspicion when Phainon, who’s stopped looking around, immediately takes the drink from him and downs it in one smooth motion. 

“Hey–”

“Damn, that’s good,” Phainon compliments before finishing his own glass with the same ease. 

“You’re going to end up in the hospital with alcohol poisoning if you keep this up,” he warns in a low voice as another unfamiliar gentleman brushes past them without sparing them a courteous glance. It’s only been a minute, and Mydei already wants to go back home. 

“It’ll be worth it. You know you can’t drink right now, so I’ll just have to make up for it,” Phainon explains. 

“That’s a terrible idea,” Mydei retorts before going to fix Phainon’s already crooked blue tie. 

“But it’s the only one that could work, unless you’re just planning to water the plants with this,” he counters back, his eyes bright with a challenge. Realizing the other man won’t give up so easily, Mydei just shuts his mouth and lets Phainon be. 

“Let’s just go, I don’t want to be around those assholes any longer than I need to.” He twitches as the whispering gets louder and grabs Phainon’s hand, pulling him up a set of curved staircases that lead to one of the beautifully decorated living rooms. There are still a few guests there chatting amongst themselves, but Mydei doesn’t notice them. 

He spots a lone familiar figure leaning against the bookshelf, nursing a cup of bourbon as he avoids mingling with the other guests. Krateros. Mydei feels a wave of relief come over him as he strides over to the man with Phainon trailing behind him. The older gentleman’s expression morphs from one of boredom to one of delighted surprise when he and Mydei lock eyes. 

“Mydeimos, my boy!” Krateros exclaims and stretches his arms out for an embrace. “You made it! I didn’t think you’d show up when your mother told me she invited you.” He claps a large, strong hand on Mydei’s back before resting it on his shoulder again when they part. “It’s been a while, how have you been?” 

“Good,” he replies. “You know, same old, same old. The cafe is still standing, lots of new patrons have been coming by lately, so I’ve been busier than usual.”

“Well, being busy is good, it means you’ve come a long way since you first opened up that little shop, Mydeimos,” Krateros starts to beam when his smile falters. “But you should also take care of yourself. Are you alright? You seem a little tired.” 

Because the little brat growing inside of me just learned how to kick and won’t stop now, Mydei thinks, but instead says, “I've just been having trouble falling asleep,” he explains half truthfully. As if on cue, the baby kicks his kidney. Ow, that one hurt. 

“Have you told your mother yet? She might have something to help with that,” Krateros offers helpfully. Mydei tries to hide his wince with a phony cough while trying not to grab at his abdomen. Hey, please behave, he silently begs as the baby refuses to settle back down. 

“Not yet, it’s just a problem that recently showed up.” He bites the inside of his cheek hard to try to keep his expression calm and clenches his fist, a cold sweat starting to form over his skin.

That’s when he feels Phainon’s hand creep up around him to cup the side of his stomach, and just like that, the baby’s movement starts to die down. Mydei lets out a relieved sigh as the discomfort slowly begins to fade before looking back at Phainon, who seems deeply concerned. He does his best to redirect the conversation away from his sudden ailment quickly. 

“Ah, Krateros, let me introduce you to Phainon. He’s my–” Roommate? Fuckbuddy? New co-parent?  

“I’m an old college classmate of Mydeimos’s,” Phainon interjects, reaching out to offer his hand to Krateros, who shakes it with a slightly confused expression before realization dawns on his face. “We ran into each other recently and got to catching up when he invited me to come along to this party.” As Phainon takes over, Mydei feels his body relax even further as the baby settles completely again.

“Wait, the same Phainon Mydei lived with during school? I remember him mentioning that same name a few times to Gorgo when they talked on the phone.” Heat floods his body as he can practically feel the large shit-eating grin forming on Phainon’s face. 

“Aw, you talked about me to your mom, Mydei? How sweet,” he coos playfully. Mydei wants to punch him, tell him to get his hands off his stomach now that the baby’s calmed down again, but just bites his lip and looks away, cheeks pink. 

“Well, anyway. It’s nice to finally meet you in person, Phainon. Thank you for being such a dear friend to Mydeimos for all these years,” Krateros praises genuinely, his eyes soft as he glances back at Mydei. “We were all so worried about him, being so far away from home. It was always a relief to hear back from him and to know that he had plenty of friends there to support and take care of him.”  

Phainon stills for a moment, stunned, before flashing a soft, earnest smile. “Of course,” he responds, pulling Mydei closer until their bodies are against each other, and Mydei can feel his breath against his ear. 

“Why don’t I get us a drink while we wait for dinner, and then we can chat some more?” Krateros suggests, slipping away again to find an attendant. Once they’re alone, Mydei slumps against the other and groans. Phainon is instantly worried, his brows creased together. 

“What’s wrong? Are you still not feeling well? You looked like you were in pain earlier,” he explains before reaching back down to massage Mydei’s abdomen gently. 

“I’m fine,” he rasps out, trying to sound reassuring as Phainon guides him to sit down in an armchair. “I guess the baby was just upset about something,” he mutters, careful to keep his voice low enough for only Phainon to hear. The other man hums, never taking his hand off Mydei’s bump. 

“I know you said you wanted to come for your mother, but we don’t have to stay if you’re not feeling well. I’m sure she’ll understand.” Mydei stubbornly shook his head. He’s gotten this far, he’ll be damned if he turns back now.

“I’ll be okay.” Phainon doesn’t look convinced, about to retort when Mydei hears a familiar voice, a voice he’s missed listening to when he still lived at home. 

“Mydeimos, you’re here.” Gorgo, in a simple, sophisticated red dress with her perfectly done dual-toned hair and makeup, almost cries at the sight of her only son sitting there right in front of her. “Oh, I’ve missed you so much.”  Mydei gets up and practically runs to her, wrapping his arms tightly around her more petite, lithe frame.

“Mother,” he croaks, the scent of her perfume bringing back childhood memories of them baking in the kitchen and playing out in the yard. He tries not to squeeze her too hard as she gently pets his hair, just like she used to whenever he was upset. “I’m home, Mother.”

Even though it had been years since Mydei left home, Gorgo could immediately see that something was different. Call it a mother’s intuition, but she can see that he hasn’t been sleeping enough, given how visible his eyebags are. His smile is also strained, no longer as carefree or relaxed as it was before. It’s almost like he’s hiding something from her. She’s a little saddened to have Mydei think he can’t tell her things, but it’s best to let him come to her and not force things out of him if he isn’t ready. 

She is thrilled to finally meet Phainon in person after hearing so much about him through Mydei’s phone calls. He’s tall, charismatic, and handsome with striking blue eyes and white hair. He’s kind, outgoing, and protective, always sticking to Mydei like a large white fluffy dog trailing after its owner; it’s a perfect contrast to Mydei’s more gruff, closed-off, guarded personality. They make an interesting pair, Gorgo thinks. 

More of Mydei’s strangeness continues; he must think he’s getting away with being discreet, but Gorgo knows. Whenever one of the attendees comes by offering them more drinks, she doesn’t miss the way her son and Phainon will switch glasses. Phainon will hastily finish his glass before slipping the empty one into Mydei’s hand, who pretends like he’s the one who enjoyed it.  They do this so many times that Gorgo is starting to see the effects of the alcohol on Phainon’s face. His face is flushed, his words are becoming more slurred as his eyelids begin to droop. Gorgo is about to cut him off when there is the announcement that dinner is served. 

Mydei steadies Phainon as the other man tries not to trip over his own feet. Mydei’s lips pressed into a tight, concerned line as they walked to the dining room together. As they approach, Gorgo sees her husband waiting for her patiently with a kind smile and starts to pull out her chair for her. She makes sure to block his view of Mydei as she leans in to give him a quick peck on the cheek.

“Happy birthday, my dear Gorgo,” Eurypon says softly when she takes her seat, pushing her in to enjoy her favorite meal, when he finally looks up and locks eyes with Mydei. Her son instantly stiffens, his jaw clenches as he tries to keep his expression neutral and blank. “Mydeimos,” Eurypon’s tone is cold and clipped with a stern, displeased gleam in his eyes. “You’re here.” Mydei’s frown grows deeper in response. 

“Mother invited me,” he explains with a voice that is equally as unfriendly. Gorgo tenses, the atmosphere around their family is too frigid and uncomfortable. She wants to stand up and scold both her husband and child, to tell them to at least try and get along for a few hours until the night was over. But she can’t, can’t force something that has no desire to change. 

“I see,” Euryphon finally answers after a pause. “Then you and your…friend should join us for dinner. We still have a few empty seats,” he remarks before gesturing to the two unoccupied spots across from Gorgo. Eurypon takes his usual seat at the head of the table. Mydei grits his teeth but flashes his mother an apologetic glance before pulling Phainon behind him. 

Gorgo knows that the night will not end well.

The atmosphere is so tense and brittle, Mydei is afraid that one single move will shatter the false peacefulness that has blanketed their end of the table. No one has said a word, focused down at their plate. Mydei feels his own hunger starting to get to him, but the sight of the large, greasy steak in front of him makes his insides turn. He tries to nibble on a little slice, but the intense spices and seasonings almost make him sick. 

Phainon isn’t faring that much better either. He’s drunk, his blue eyes are hazy and unfocused, even though he tries to keep up the facade. Eurypon, who is sitting next to Mydei, doesn’t even try to engage in conversation with him, so Phainon is left to chat with his mother, who he’s pretty sure knows something isn’t right. He can feel his father's disapproving glare burning holes into him as Mydei picks at his steak. He takes another big gulp of water and tries to get at least a bite down when Eurypon decides to open his stupid mouth. 

“The food not up to your ridiculous standards? This is some of the finest cuts in Castrum Kremnos, and you won’t even touch it,” he says coolly. Gorgo pauses to shoot her husband a disapproving glare. Mydei grits his teeth.

“No,” he replies curtly, his fingers tightening around the handle of the steak knife. “That’s not it, I’m just not that hungry,” he lies, but Eurypon doesn’t stop. 

“Then what, do you still think all of this is still too good for you?” Mydei slams his utensils down on the table, startling all four of them. 

“Eurypon,” Mydei’s mother warns him in a stern voice, but both men are too worked up. He can feel his frustration tearing up behind his eyes, forming a knot in his throat. He barks a cold, sardonic laugh. 

“You’d wish it was something like that, wouldn’t you, old man?” he spits. His father leans back in his chair, unfazed. Mydei wants nothing more than to slam his fist into the old dick’s face, break his nose. 

“Well, if it’s not that, then what is it? What can I do to earn my sweet, soft, gentle son’s affections? Earn the same type of love his mother has?” The old business tycoon moans melodramatically. “Has none of the sacrifices we’ve made, all those years of trying to mold you into something that will be remembered, gone to waste.” His voice is cruel, heartless, like a knife stabbing and twisting into Mydei’s heart. “Go on, throw the plate away just like you did to all those opportunities I gave to try and make you a better man. It’s all gone to waste already, why not just add to the pile.” 

All Mydei sees is red, the rush of his blood roaring in his ears. He starts to get up out of his seat when something shocking happens. 

Phainon stands up so abruptly that the table shakes when his legs hit the edge. His blue eyes are burning, wide and delirious with rage as he points an accusatory finger right at Mydei’s father. “You–” he snarls, his fists balled up tightly. “You take that back right now. How dare you speak to Mydei that way!” Eurypon, alarmed at first, chuckles in cold amusement. 

“And who the hell are you, telling me what I can and can’t say about my own son. He might be a grown man, but he will always be my child.” He even takes a sip from his wine glass, the whole party now turned to them, watching with scandalized expressions. Eurypon’s golden eyes gleam with a challenge as he turns to address Mydei again. 

“You really know how to choose them, Mydemios. You’ll certainly have a bright future ahead of you.” He laughs. “A very bright one indeed.” Mydei wants to throw up. He should never have accepted the invitation. He glances over at his poor mother, who looks like she’s on the verge of tears. But Phainon, still inebriated, doesn’t back down. 

“Oh, believe me, we will. Far away from you. Our baby will never learn about you and the way you treated your own family. They will never see your face or know your name, because that’s the least you deserve,” Phainon fulminates. “Mydei is an amazing man, the best one I know and the fact that you can’t see that because your head is so far up your own ass is such a fucking shame. You don’t deserve to have him as a son, and he sure as hell never should have had you as a father.” 

“What did he just say?”

“Did I hear that right?”

“He said, our baby. Mydeimos is pregnant!?” 

Whispers and murmurs erupt, and there are suddenly too many eyes on him. Eurypon’s mouth falls open, and Gorgo’s eyes are wide. It’s too much all at once, and Mydei can’t handle it anymore. He needs to get out. 

He grabs Phainon’s hand and runs out of there, not once looking back as they run out of the mansion, towards the car. He tosses drunk Phainon into the back seat and tears out of there, his childhood home disappearing in the rearview mirror as he floors it. 

Once he’s out of the private driveway and back on the main road, he hysterically laughs until all he has left are sobs. 

“I messed up big time, didn’t I?” Phainon slurs as Mydei helps him into bed, his hair wet and dripping after the quick shower the baker gave him before changing him into his comfy pajamas. “I’m sorry, Dei. Please don’t kick me out.” During the long drive back, Mydei was able to calm down and think a little more clearly. While it wasn’t at all how he wanted to tell his mother about his pregnancy, it’s too late now. Mydei sighs and pulls the blankets up around Phainon. 

“Idiot, I’m not going to punish the guy who stuck their neck out for me like that,” he says softly, sitting down next to him on the edge of the bed. He pushes back those soft white bangs away from Phainon’s eyes and cups his cheek, rubbing his thumb reassuringly across his flushed skin. Phainon doesn’t hesitate to lean into Mydei’s palm, nuzzling his fingers sweetly. 

Something in Mydei’s chest jumps at that, his face now hot for an entirely different reason. He couldn’t believe Phainon did that, said all the things Mydei had always wanted to say to his father. He did so with such reckless abandon, not caring about what everyone else thought of him because all that mattered to Phainon was…him, Mydei. He withdraws his hand and starts to get up again when Phainon whines and grabs his wrist.

“No, don’t leave me,” he whimpers, watery blue eyes staring pleadingly up at him. 

“I’m just going to get you some aspirin and water and maybe a wastebasket to throw up into,” Mydei tries to reassure him and tries to pry the other man’s fingers apart, but Phainon stubbornly clings on. 

“No, Mydei. Please stay.” Actual tears roll down his face as Phainon hiccups. It’s so pathetic and adorable that Mydei heaves out another sigh and stays. He pets through those soft, white tresses and wipes away Phainon’s tears. 

“Dumbass, what am I going to do with you,” he asks aloud. 

“Don’t be mad at me,” Phainon pouts. 

“I’m not mad,” Mydei promises. “I’m…relieved. Thank you, Phainon. For everything you said. It…it really means a lot.” Phainon hums back in sleepy agreement, his eyes now fully closed. In the lamp’s warm, golden light, he looks beautiful, ethereal. Mydei can’t hold himself back any longer. 

“Hey, Phainon?”

“Hm?”

“Can I kiss you?” His eyes shot open again, startling Mydei from his precarious position on the bed, his cheeks flushed. 

“What did you just say?” Mydei looks away, mortified. After all their years of casual sex, hook-ups, and fleeting touches, asking for a kiss should be the most innocent thing to ask for. So then, why does it feel like Mydei’s been lit on fire?

“I said–” he gulps, “Can I kiss you?” Phainon sits up, his drunken expression openly happy and excited. 

“I..i-if you’re sure. I’m okay with anything you wanna do, Dei. I can’t–” Mydei cuts him off, surging forward to press his lips against Phainon’s soft pink ones, the last of alcohol still on his tongue. It’s bitter, but Mydei doesn’t mind. It just feels right to him. Phainon kisses him back eagerly and sloppily, just like an overly excited dog. 

“Phainon,” Mydei murmurs between their lips, finding himself slowly becoming addicted to the taste and feel of Phainon’s plush pink lips. Mydei doesn’t realize he’s closed his eyes until he feels the other man go slack and unresponsive, opening his eyes again to see Phainon passed out asleep. 

He’s already drooling all over his pillow, the smallest smile teasing the sides of his lips. Mydei huffs in amusement and runs a hand through his messy mane of hair, his tongue and lips tingling with warmth. 

“Seriously, what am I going to do with you?” he chuckles affectionately before taking his usual spot in the bed, curled up against Phainon’s back with his arms wrapped around the other man’s waist. He buries his nose into the crook of Phainon’s neck and falls asleep with the familiar scent of their shampoo in his nose.

Chapter End Notes

Chapter Summary

Mydei and Phainon finally have a moment together 😏.

And a twist at the end.

Chapter Notes

I'm not ready for the new update. I haven't even finished the story yet bc I'm not at all prepared for the pain that's coming my way. Send help, lolol. Also, sorry if there is some OOC, I was too excited lol

Anyway, here's a super long chapter! I hope you enjoy! We're officially more than halfway done! :)

“So, let me get this straight. He got drunk for you, stood up to your dad by verbally giving him the middle finger, and then you kissed him. Am I hearing this right? Did I leave anything else out?” 

Mydei just wordlessly nibbles on the oak cake his friends bought for him. Hephaestion stares at him with a long, silent, long-suffering stare before letting out an equally weary sigh. The rest of their friends stopped what they were doing. Ptolemy and Leonnius’s own conversation was put on pause as both of them turned to stare wide-eyed and slack-jawed at him. Peucesta cackled like a hyena, accidentally startling the pets, and Perdikkas just shook his head and looked equally exhausted.

“Oh, sweet clueless Mydei,” Peucesta gasps in between fits of laughter, “If you don’t lock that poor man down soon, I will.” Mydei chokes suddenly.

“What?” he rasps while coughing, some of his drink dribbling down his chin. 

“Dude, he defended your honor against one of the biggest, most powerful men in Castrum Kremnos and embarrassed him in front of all his friends. That’s like things you only hear about in fairy tales and in those stupid trashy romance novels Lemy secretly likes to read,” Leonnius chimes in. 

“Hey,” Ptolemy complains, punching the other man in the shoulder. “They aren’t trashy, you’re just shit at talking to women.” Lennius flips him off, but Hephaestion butts in before they could continue. 

“Anyway, before we get even more off topic here…Mydei, you didn’t answer my question. Is there anything else you haven’t told us?” Curse Hephaestion and his scary sixth sense of knowing when there’s more trouble. 

“He doesn’t remember what happened,” Mydei reluctantly mumbles around a mouthful of cake, silently hoping that they didn’t hear him and would drop the subject. But of course, the opposite happened. 

“What?!” Peucesta screeched, the musician’s usually calming and soothing voice high-pitched and scratchy. 

“I mean, he remembers most of that night. He said he can recall most of the party and his outburst to my father, but the kiss…he doesn’t remember anything else after we left.” Mydei can still feel the remnants of the hurt left behind when he and Phainon talked the next morning, the physician still a little hungover as he did his best to relive the previous events.  

Lennonius stands up and grabs his coat, his expression furious. Ptolemy starts to join him.  “Where is he right now? At the clinic? It doesn’t matter; Perdikkas probably knows which one. I can send him a quick message, then he’ll surely remember–”

“Leon, no,” Mydei hastily interjects, Hephaestion reaching out to stop the runner. “I-it’s fine. Really.” No one looks convinced. “It was mostly just a spur-of-the-moment thing; it wasn’t serious.”  For a moment, there is nothing but terrible, suffocating silence. 

“Are you sure about, Mydeimos?” Hephaestion finally speaks, breaking the stillness after what feels like hours. He lets go of Lennonius to take Mydei’s hands in his, gently rubbing his thumb over the knobs of Mydei’s knuckles. “To be honest, it doesn’t sound like you are.” 

“What do you mean?” he asks, his brows furrowing in confusion. 

“Well, for starters, you’re having this man’s baby. The two of you are living together again. He’s been waiting on you hand and foot while also taking care of the pets, attending every doctor’s appointment, even bringing you back home to meet his parents, and now this. This doesn’t sound like the casual relationship you said you wanted anymore, Mydei.” Hephaestion painstakingly points out.   

His friends all nod in agreement. “Look, the two of you already act like you’ve been married for years,” Ptolemy adds. 

“Even more so now that we’ve all seen and heard about how madly in love with you Phainon is.” 

“He isn’t in love with me,” Mydei instantly counters, to which Perdikkas snorts in laughter.
