“I understand,” she answered after a beat of tense silence with a small, sad smile. “I thought about visiting and telling him myself, but I couldn’t. I didn’t want to disturb the peace he’s built for himself.” Her eyes gleamed with an indescribable emotion as she took Phainon’s hand in between hers. 

“If you do tell him, please do so gently. He has always been a kind and gentle boy. I don’t want him to think that this was his fault,” she said softly as Phainon helped her down from the bench.

“I’ll try. But you know, he’s a lot tougher than you think. He just wants you to be happy,” Phainon reassured, doing his best to reassure her as he helped her off the patient bench and walked her to the front desk. 

Her shoulders were still tense, but her smile was still genuine. “I know,” she reciprocated. Before she left, she even gave Phainon a warm hug. “I’m delighted to see that he’s found someone who truly understands him and cares about him. I hope your future together remains as bright as ever.”)

“It’s most definitely a surprise, 

Phainon, who has his head nestled in Mydei’s lap, turns his face back up to answer when he stares right at the baker’s magnificent naked chest. He's seen them before many times, even knows them by feel… but has Mydei’s chest gotten…bigger? They seemed squishier, more prominent. Phainon gulps, his mouth suddenly going dry. Mydei also notices him stiffening and peers down at him curiously. 

“Something wrong?” he inquires with an arched eyebrow. 

“No, it’s nothing serious. Just um…,” Phainon stammers, not able to look away from those squishy mounds. “Haveyourboobsgottenbigger?” he finally blurts out, embarrassment running hot through his body just as Mydei blushes a lovely shade of pink. The man above him stutters and grits his teeth.

“...I-they’re…lactating,” Mydei mutters under his breath before looking away again. Phainon blinks; his mind goes full blue screen. “I noticed it this morning when I was getting dressed. Ruined the shirt I sleep in,” he continues to mutter under his breath before Phainon finally sits back up, his eyes now glued to the other’s naked chest, and without thinking, flat out asks:

“Can I…try some?”

“...”

“HSK! Get away from me, you disgusting pig!”

Mydei nervously glances at the clock hanging over the door to the shop, his finger impatiently tapping on the table. Phainon reaches out to hold his fidgeting hand, even though the baker can feel the slight tremble in his palm. 

Krateros has always been a punctual person, rarely late, and when he was, the older man would always call ahead to inform the other party. So why, twenty minutes past their agreed-upon time at Mydei’s cafe, has he not arrived yet?

“Maybe he couldn’t find a good parking spot?” Phainon offers out rather dumbly, but Mydei is too tense to rebuke that ridiculousness, considering that the street parking just a few buildings down was pretty vacant. He feels the baby kick against the walls of his stomach as if the babe itself had gotten impatient with waiting when the door suddenly swings open, revealing a surprisingly out-of-breath Krateros. 

“Mydeimos, my boy, I’m so sorry for being late! I meant to call and tell you, but I realized that my phone was dead, so I ran from my car as fast as I could!” the older gentleman explains as he sits down at the table across from the couple. He smiles warmly at Mydei, his whiskered face pink with exertion. 

“Let me go and get you some water, sir. I’ll leave you two to catch up,” Phainon suggests, leaving Mydei’s side to run into the back kitchen. It’s one of the only few times he’ll let Phainon into the kitchen unsupervised because how hard is it to get water? Krateros gives him a polite, close-lipped smile and thanks him before turning his attention back to Mydei. 

“So,” he starts to say, his dark eyes wandering down to his uncovered round belly. “How are you? What have the doctors said? Is everything going…?” Krateros drifts off just as Mydei feels the baby stir as if on cue; he tries not to wince when he gets another good-aimed kick to his kidneys (Mydei’s pretty sure that they’re going to be permanently bruised by this point).  

“Everything seems to be going well. Baby’s healthy and active. Maybe a little too active,” he mutters mostly to himself, but Krateros hears it and lets out a chuckle. Mydei flushes. 

“I still remember your mother saying the same thing when she was pregnant with you.” He glances down at Mydei’s hand, now resting on top of his bump. “Do you know what you’re having?” 

“It’s a boy,” Mydei explains, a ting of excitement and happiness as he recalls the latest visit to the doctor’s office earlier that week. Phainon had burst into happy tears when they were told and hugged Mydei so hard that the nurses were worried that he was going to break the pregnant man’s ribs. “We’ve been thinking of names since we learned.” 

“I see, that’s wonderful news, congratulations,” Krateros compliments just as Phainon comes back with drinks, a glass of water for Krateros and a cup of his favorite pomegranate tea for Mydei before taking his usual spot right next to Mydei, reaching for his other hand under the table. Mydei lets their joyous moment linger in the air before finally bracing himself and asking the more important question:

“How is my mother doing?” he asks quietly while squeezing Phainon’s hand. Krateros pauses before taking a sip of water. His brows are furrowed, his expression now tinged with an aura of sadness. 

“She’s fine, just a little tired from all that’s been happening, but she’s settling down nicely at the townhouse,” Krateros reports. “She’s picked up baking again and said she’s even come up with some new recipes she’d like for you to try.” It’s a poorly veiled excuse for Mydei to visit her, but he doesn’t mind. He feels a rush of excitement at the idea of seeing her again, just the two of them, without the looming presence of his father. Speaking of which–

“I haven’t seen him since Gorgo asked me to help her move out. According to the rumors circulating, he’s been keeping himself locked up in his office and hasn’t been seen since the party.” Krateros catches the condensation dewing on the sides of his glass. “I tried to call him at first, but every single one has been rejected, or he has his secretary taking them.” 

Mydei doesn’t react; just stares down at his cup of red tea. It’s strange; he doesn’t necessarily feel bad for his father, but at the same time, he doesn’t feel that vindication he thought he’d always get when Eurypon finally got what was coming to him. Why didn’t he feel that? Why did he suddenly feel a strange surge of pity for the same man who’s done nothing but spew hurtful insults and tore Mydei down at every given opportunity?

“Mydei, are you alright?” Phainon asks, concerned. His voice snaps Mydei out of his conflicted stupor.

“Yeah, I’m fine.” He takes a large gulp of his hot tea, almost scalding his tongue and throat in the process. He can feel Phainon’s disbelieving frown burning into his profile, but he ignores it for now. “Does anyone at the company know the real reason as to why my father’s acting this way?”

“No, as far as the company is aware, they think Eurypon is just trying to recover and save face from Phainon’s outburst at the party.” Said man coughs awkwardly as he tries not to fidget with embarrassment. Krateros doesn’t seem too upset with him; in fact, his expression is completely neutral as he studies Phainon from head to toe. 

“So no one knows about the divorce?” Mydei asks, diverting Krateros’s attention back to him (he can feel Phainon relax against his side again). 

“No, your mother’s determined to keep the proceedings as quiet and private as possible. Luckily, it seems like your father isn’t putting up much of a fight either. I had dinner with her a few nights ago, and she said he’s signed and sent over his portion of the agreement.” 

Wait, he and Gorgo, his mother , were having dinner together?! Mydei almost drops his teacup out of surprise. Gorgo had always had a closer relationship with Krateros than Eurypon did, even after the couple had gotten married, mainly since they had grown up together. But could it be possible? 

His eyes widen as he stares at the man sitting across the table from him, realization dawning over him. Krateros has picked up on his shift as well because his expression morphs into one of shock. He’s about to defend himself when Mydei cuts him off.

“Krateros,” he asks slowly, “Are you and my mother…?” 

“No! I mean, I would never do something like that!” Mydei’s disbelief then swiftly turns to anger and offense. 

“What, why not? Is my mother not good enough for you?” he growls, startling and confusing the two other men. Phainon frowns as Krateros flounders, embarrassed and unsure of how to remedy this conversation.

“No, it’s not that! I mean, of course, your mother is a wonderful woman. Kind, smart, and beautiful, anyone would be lucky to be with her!” Krateros tries to defend himself hurriedly. Phainon, after figuring out what was going on, does his best to cover up his snickering by looking away. 

“Then what’s the problem?” Mydei snarls, ignoring the muffled giggles shaking Phainon’s figure. 

“I couldn’t possibly…at this time,” Krateros stammers, to which Phainon finally intervenes, no longer able to hold back his amusement. 

“Mydei, baby, calm down,” Phainon giggles while placing a hand on Mydei’s tense arm. “It’s okay; Krateros is just being a good friend to your mother, nothing more. He was just trying to explain how it would be improper for him to romantically pursue her, just as she’s going through the whole process with your dad.” Krateros, still a little pale and shaken, just eagerly nods along. 

“You must know, Mydeimos, that I would never do something so scandalous. Especially when she’s in such a vulnerable spot,” Krateros adds. Phainon continues to rub soothing circles over Mydei’s back until he finally relaxes and starts to think clearly. He’s usually more rational than that, not as prone to emotional outbursts like that just now (it was usually Phainon who was the more emotional one between them).  Embarrassment then surges through him, and he feels his face heat up with mortification as he tries to gather himself again. 

“Of course, I know that. I just– I deeply apologize for my outburst, Krateros. I don’t know what came over me,” he coughs awkwardly before looking back down at his empty cup. Fortunately, the older man is a little more patient than usual because he just shrugs off Mydei’s concern with a small smile. 

“It’s alright. Your mother went through the very same mood swings when she was pregnant with you. One time, she yelled at Eurypon and me for breathing too loudly, and within the same hour, she was crying over not finding a particular drink she wanted,” Krateros chuckles fondly, his wrinkled face warm as he reminisces. He then looks over at Phainon with a stern but still amused expression. 

“If he’s going to be anything like his mother, I’m afraid you’ll have your work cut out for you, Phainon Khaslana.” He and Phainon chuckle while Mydei just wishes the Earth would swallow him whole at this point. 

“Don’t worry,” Phainon comforts as he wraps an arm around Mydei’s shoulders, pulling the baker close to his side. “I’ll be able to handle anything you throw my way.”

It’s in the middle of the night when Phainon’s woken up to the sound of Mydei quietly sobbing next to him. Alarm jolts him out of his drowsy slumber as he rolls over to cradle the man to his chest. He gently shushes Mydei as he pets a hand through the dual-colored locks, “What’s wrong, Mydei? Are you in pain? Do you want me to give you a massage?” With his face pressed against Phainon’s hard pecs, Mydei shakes his head repeatedly. 

“I want Immortal’s Delight,” he says, his voice trembling with each sob. Phainon doesn’t say anything at first as he reaches over and grabs his phone. It’s in the middle of the night, so none of the stores are open, but Phainon can’t tell Mydei that, lest he wants to make the pregnant man have an even bigger meltdown.  

“Okay, that’s okay. I can make some for you if you'd like. I think we still have some of those milk tea packets in the pantry. And I know we still have some extra tapioca pearls from the shop,” he starts to reassure, hoping that it’ll be enough to soothe Mydei’s craving. But much to his shock, the suggestion only makes him more upset as he cries harder.

“No, it won’t be right. It has to be the one from The Sleepless Earl,” Mydei growls back through his tears as if Phainon had just personally insulted his entire bloodline. More angry tears streak down his face, “I know the store is closed, but it’s all I can think about right now, and I…” he chokes off with another frustrated sniffle. Phainon doesn’t pull away and continues to try to soothe him while thinking up some alternatives that might work.

“It’s going to be okay, Mydei. Don’t cry; I’ll come up with something. Hey, I’m sure there have to be some drink recipes online that are similar to the one from The Sleepless Earl. Why don’t we try to look for a few and see if they’re any good? If they’re not, I promise, first thing in the morning, I’ll drive down there and get you their biggest cup.  How does that sound?” Phainon offers. After a couple more sniffles, Mydei finally nods. 

Relieved, Phainon starts searching for imitation Immortal’s Delight recipes on his phone until he finds one that seems pretty similar to the ones found at the teashop. He shows the screen to Mydei, who fortunately seems to have stopped crying long enough to deem the find as a worthy try. It takes Phainon a while to get out of bed simply because Mydei refuses to let go. 

They end up with a compromise: Phainon will do the cooking while Mydei guides and babysits on the sidelines. It’s the first time Phainon’s been allowed to cook in the kitchen, and even though the recipe is exceedingly easy, he’s still worried about messing up. 

Mydei watches him like a hawk as Phainon stirs the tea and cream on the stovetop, making sure that it simmers and doesn’t boil before going to start on the tapioca pearls. He hadn’t realized just how sugary the drink was until he started making it. Still, Phainon didn’t complain as he spooned in the correct amount of brown sugar needed for the syrup. 

Once all the ingredients are independently ready, Phainon spoons the sticky, gooey balls into a cup before pouring in the tea. It looks pretty close to The Sleepless Earl’s, so when he offers the mug to Mydei, the baker carefully studies the beverage before taking a small sip. Phainon waits with bated breath.

“So, how is it?” he asks nervously as Mydei continues to savor the drink, his expression unrecognizable before he downs it all eagerly.

“It’s…good,” Mydei finally answers, staring sadly at his now-empty cup. He wants more, Phainon realizes, and can’t help but chuckle.

Cute, he thinks to himself as he refills the baker’s cup to the brim with more boba tea. When Mydei offers to share, he politely declines. “It’s a little too sweet for my taste.” A little hesitant, Mydei frowns. 

“But you made it, and there’s so much of it left over,” he mumbles, suddenly bashful as he looks back at the half-full pot of tea. Phainon just smiles. 

“It’s okay, we can save the rest for later,” Phainon suggests before refilling his cup. Mydei looks like he wants to object but decides not to, finishing off another cup before letting Phainon clean up.

He pours the rest of the tea into a pitcher and places the remaining boba into an airtight container before washing the dishes and putting them away. At the same time, Mydei makes sure the animals’ water bowl is full before the two climb back into bed. Phainon curls up next to Mydei, his head resting on the baker’s chest while Mydei runs his fingers through his pale hair.   

“Thank you for indulging me. You know I’m not usually like this, and I’m sorry for dragging you out in the middle of the night,” Mydei mumbles as he turns around to wrap his arms around Phainon. “I don’t know what came over me.”

“It’s alright,” Phainon comforts him, brushing Mydei’s long hair away from his face to kiss his forehead. He feels a pang of guilt when he notices how puffy the other man’s eyes are. “I know that it’s just the pregnancy hormones. I don’t mind,” he tries to reassure the other, but the glimmer of hesitancy still lingers in Mydei’s golden eyes. 

“Still, it was just a hassle.” Phainon shakes his head. 

“Hey, don’t say that. It’s not a hassle; it’s the least I can do, especially considering what you’re doing for us. It doesn’t come close to the fact that you’re growing and carrying a whole person inside of you.” He reaches down to gently cup the baby bump, feeling their baby boy kick against his palm. Phainon smiles. “Even if it means getting up in the middle of the night to make you your favorite dessert, I’d do it a million times over.” He hears Mydei sniffle again, fresh tears starting to cling to his long eyelashes. Phainon bites the inside of his cheek to keep from giggling as he wipes the baker’s eyes dry. 

“You’re such a disgusting sap,” Mydei mutters as Phainon leans in to kiss him, the sweet notes of milk tea and brown sugar heavy on the baker’s tongue. Still embarrassed, he buries his face into the side of Phainon’s neck. He wordlessly wraps his arms tightly around Mydei, a slight smile on his face as they drift off again.

“I have to say, you’re handling all of this well for a first-time, expecting father,” Cyrene tells him one afternoon on his day off. Mydei is downstairs managing the cafe with Hephaestion. Phainon snorts and pokes his head out of the kitchen (he’s started to learn the basics from Mydei after he realizes that Phainon might have to do a lot of cooking when the baby comes. So far, he’s mastered the art of making the perfect grilled cheese) “I thought he’d kick you out as soon you burnt one of his favorite pans.”  

“Thanks for the vote of confidence there, Cyrene,” he jokingly retorts while the pink-haired woman just smiles back cheekily. Phainon finishes making up their lunch before joining her in the living room, where Cyrene gently nudges Bubbles and Leo away from their plates. 

“Hey, you can’t blame me for being a little on the cautious side,” she jokes back. Despite her teasing words, Phainon knows she means well. And if he’s happy and content with Mydei, that’s enough to ease the rest of Cyrene’s concern. After they have lunch, they chat for a bit longer before taking Bubbles out for his second daily walk to the nearby park. 

It’s a beautiful autumn day; the sky is mostly clear, with a few fluffy white clouds hanging overhead, and a pleasant breeze keeps them from getting too hot as they sit on a park bench. He takes a few pictures of Bubbles frolicking, eating grass, and playing with other dogs and sends a few of them to Mydei. The baker doesn’t reply, most likely busy with the cafe, so Phainon just pockets his phone again and turns to Cyrene. 

“Ugh, I wish you’d stop looking like that,” she groans in faux annoyance. 

“Like what?” Phainon asks innocently as if he doesn’t know already. He even tits his head to the side like Bubbles when he’s confused. 

“Like a puppy dog that’s just waiting for his owner to come home,” she remarks. “I knew you were already done bad, but I never realized just how bad it was.” Phainon blushes. “Don't forget to bring me along when you go wedding dress shopping.”

“Hey, I’m not that bad,” he exclaims, lying loudly, like a liar. 

“Oh please, have you forgotten that I was once on the phone with you for five hours because Mydei cuddled you in bed, and you freaked out? Because I still remember, “Cyrene starts to number them off, much to Phainon’s horror. “Or what about that time you called me crying because he canceled on a ‘study date’, or when you came back after class and saw him wearing your hoodie? That was a fun conversation. I learned a lot about Mydei then, a little more than I’d like–”

“Okay, okay, I get it!” Phainon quickly throws a hand over her mouth to get her to stop talking and to save himself from any further embarrassment. Fine, so maybe he was just a little obsessed with Mydei, but how could he not? He’s beautiful, intelligent, talented, and kind; anyone would be lucky to have him in their life. 

“Why are you bringing this up now? I thought you’d be happy for me,” Phainon asks, suddenly curious now. Cyrene shrugs her shoulders, but the troubled light in her bright blue eyes doesn’t dim. 

“I am. Don’t get me wrong, I’m so excited for you and Mydei. You guys are having a freaking baby. That’s huge, but–” she pauses, carefully thinking over her following words. “You know I love you, and I know how you wear your heart on your sleeve. I just don’t want to see you get hurt if things don’t work out.” 

“I know, and I love you too, Cyrene,” he replies. His smile is warm as he tries to reassure her. “I really appreciate you looking out for me, but...” he trails off, recalling the warmth in Mydei’s eyes as Phainon talks to their son and takes care of their animals, his handsome face slack with sleep as he lies in Phainon’s arms. 

“I’ve known him for years, ever since we met in our first year of college. He would never try to hurt me like that on purpose,” Phainon answers firmly, his heart beating loudly in his chest. Cyrene doesn’t respond at first; her expression is patient and thoughtful as she studies his face. Finally, after what seemed like hours, she breaks into a gentle smile.

“Okay, I believe you. If he truly makes you happy, that’s all I want.” Phaninon squeezes her hand and returns her reassuring smile. 

“Thank you, Cyrene,” he whispers back. 

“Yes, thanks to both of you for such a touching scene. I wouldn’t be interrupting anything, would I?” A familiar deep voice approaches them from behind, causing Phainon to spin around in surprise. It’s Mydei, his arms crossed over his chest as he watches them.

“Mydei!” Phainon exclaims before shooting up from his spot on the bench and going around to reach for the baker. “I thought you were still working at the cafe.” 

“Hephaestion forced me to take a break before closing, so I decided to swing by the park and see what you were up to,” he explains before his gaze falls on Cyrene again, who waves back at him. 

“It’s good to see you again, Mydeimos. How are you doing? How’s the baby boy coming along?” Cyrene greets him a little awkwardly. They’re on friendly terms, but she’s definitely not as close to him as Phainon is. Mydei gives her a polite nod. 

“Pretty well. He’s growing along well, although the brat won’t stop treating my insides like his own personal punching bag,” the baker replies. “How are your classes? Phainon mentioned that you got accepted into the master's program this semester.”  Phainon calls Bubbles over, making sure to leash the dog firmly before the large dog tries to jump on Mydei. “Aerospace, right? That’s a tough field.” 

“It’s manageable as long as you can keep up with the assignments,” Cyrene answers. “I was near the top of my undergrad class, so I’m not too concerned about falling behind.” 

“That’s good to hear; I wish you luck in your studies,” Mydei replies honestly before checking his watch. “It’s getting to be rather late. Phainon, would you rather we eat out or try to find something back at home?” he asks. The breeze cools as the sun sets, and people begin to head home. Phainon shrugs off his hoodie to drape it over Mydei’s shoulders as the baker takes Bubbles from him. 

“We can try that new restaurant that opened last week, the one you said that the sausages looked good at?” Phainon suggests after adjusting the jacket to fit around Mydei properly. “What do you think? How does that sound? Baby, what about you?” he teases while cupping the bump. Mydei scoffs but doesn’t brush him off like he usually does when Phainon tries to talk to the baby in public. 

“You’re welcome to join us if you’d like, Cyrene,” Mydei adds, but the young woman shakes her head and gets up as well.

“That’s very kind of you to ask, but I still have to finish this paper for school.  I’ll see you around, Phainon, and enjoy your date,” she bids them goodbye before heading in the opposite direction. Mydei and Phainon then walk out of the park, Bubbles obediently walking in step with them. 

Mydei loops his arm through Phainon’s, the sweet scent of cinnamon and honey wafting off of him whenever he presses his body against Phainon’s, Bubble’s leash in his other hand. The city’s warm yellow light bounces off his smooth skin and highlights his blond hair. Phainon almost forgets how to breathe with each secretive glance at him. 

“Hey, Mydei,” he finally says, pulling both him and Bubbles to the side to let a family walk past. “Have you thought of any names for the baby yet?” 

“A few, what about you?” Mydei replies after a contemplative pause. 

“Hundreds,” Phainon counters with a smug look, but Mydei just scoffs. “I can list them off for you if you want.”

“You and your competitiveness. I just hope the kid doesn’t inherit that from us,” he snorts jokingly. “Alright, let’s hear them. I can’t wait to veto every single one.” Phainon doesn’t complain as he shakes his head and just laughs.

“Mydei, have you ever considered moving into a bigger house?” Audata asks one afternoon when the two of them are out shopping for baby clothes. He had just been eyeing a set of incredibly adorable pajamas when Phainon’s mother asked him that question. With just two months left before his projected due date, they invited Phainon’s parents to their place in Okehma to help set up the baby’s nursery and buy some baby supplies. 

He pauses to think about his answer. He has looked at a few houses outside the city and considered moving into a larger, more family-oriented area. His apartment is lovely; it was perfect for just him and Leo. However, after Phainon and Bubbles moved in, the lack of space soon became apparent. And as the baby’s due date approaches, the city seems louder and less safe. 

“I have,” he answers honestly while picking out an adorable onesie set with firetrucks. There’s one listing he keeps thinking about and going back to: a beautiful country-style two-story house with a large fenced-in backyard and a garage with a balcony overlooking it. It’s a bit pricey, but with just his savings and the money he’s earned from the cafe and bookstore, Mydi could easily afford it on his own. Audata doesn’t reply at first but gives him an understanding smile. 

“If you two do decide to have more children, buying a family home is a good idea,” she says. Honestly, he does want more kids, a big family. Mydei adores children with their sweet, gummy smiles, their bright, round, innocent eyes, and their endless bounds of curiosity. He gives out small treats to the children and offers discounted drinks to their tired parents who come into his store, while also ensuring there are enough picture books in the children’s section.

He always pictured having at least three children, their large, round eyes full of light and warmth as he held their chubby hands, kissed their scraped knees, and read them bedtime stories. He’d bake their birthday cakes, teach them traditional Kremnoan phrases, and watch them as they graduated from college. He imagines a happy life with his family, a life filled with nothing but love and security. 

 As Mydei picks up another set of baby outfits (this one has lions on it), he turns to show Audata when he realizes that she’s disappeared from his side. He looks around, trying to find her by her pale silver hair, when another strange voice calls out his name. He spins around to see a strangely familiar brunette man with a cocky smile speed-walking towards him. 

He’s wearing these ridiculous round, dark sunglasses, even though they're inside. His hands are in his pockets, and he still has that trademark cocky smirk as he approaches Mydei. What was his name again? Scout? 

“Yo, Mydei! It’s been a while,” the strange man confidently remarks as he gets closer with one hand raised. With the infant clothes still in hand, Mydei uses them to cover his very noticeable bump before reluctantly letting the weird man pull him into an awkward bro hug. He breathes in the man’s thick cologne, almost gagging as the thick scent invades his nose.

The scent suddenly brings back a suppressed memory from his college days, back when he hooked up with any person that happened to glance in his direction. His name is Skott, a business major whose dream was to work for the IPC. They hooked up in an empty bathroom stall at a nightclub, a disappointing encounter that didn’t even last five minutes. Mydei never spoke to him again outside of their elective classes, so he isn’t sure why the businessman is greeting him like an old friend instead of an acquaintance. 

“I haven’t heard from you since graduation. How have you been?” Mydei tries not to recoil as Skott throws an arm over his shoulder, silently gripping the baby clothes tightly in his hand. 

“Fine,” he replies curtly, clenching his jaw and brows furrowed. Unfortunately, it seems Skott is still too oblivious and big-headed to notice Mydei’s cues. 

“It’s a shame that after graduation, we drifted apart. I’ve been in Amphoreus for almost a month, and we still haven’t hung out yet. I know no one here except for you.” He sighs melodramatically and runs a hand through his stiff brown hair.

He gets up to get fresh, clean socks for Mydei’s cold feet after prompting him to not move from his spot on the couch. Phainon makes sure to grab his favorite pair before returning, kneeling before Mydei as he gingerly pulls the soft, thick material up to his calves. 

Mydei tries to speak up as Phainon helps him up, but the pale-haired man shushes him. He helps the pregnant man back onto his feet, wrapping his arm around the baker’s waist as he guides them back to the bedroom. Once they settle back into bed, Phainon immediately curls up behind him with his arm firmly locked around the baker’s waist as he reaches over to switch off the lamp again. 

He can feel Mydei shifting around in his arms, fidgety and nervous, which is extremely unlike him. Phainon tries to help by cradling his stomach, but it does nothing to cease the baker’s movements. Finally, both men give up and settle in for what is now doubt going to be a tense conversation. Phainon slowly lets go just as Mydei starts to turn back around to face him. 

The baker’s expression is tight and pinched, but the gleam in his eyes reveals his determination. “Are you still mad at me?” he asks hesitantly. Phainon instantly shakes his head. 

“Not mad, just very worried,” he corrects. 

“Still, I’m sorry,” Mydei insists. Phainon squeezes him tighter to his side in reassurance. 

“So, do you want to tell me what’s going on?” he pushes gently, doing his best to sound reassuring and neutral. Phainon doesn’t want to scare or make Mydei more nervous than he probably feels now. 

“I–” Mydei starts to say before trailing off again. Phainon doesn’t stop his reassuring touches, rubbing circles along the baker’s back as he tries to find his words again. 

“Are you nervous about the delivery? It’s going to be okay. Hyacine has already vouched for Dr. Bailu’s office hundreds of times, and we’ve seen her the entire time. There’s nothing to worry about, both you and Apollo are going to be in good hands,” Phainon speaks softly, the swell of where their son is resting presses against Phainon’s abs. 

“It’s not the delivery that I’m worried about, it’s what happens after,” Mydei finally mumbles out awkwardly.  Phainon frowns, confused. Mydei takes a deep breath, his expression slowly morphing into one of worry. “I don’t know how to be a father, I mean, the one I had was nothing but a self-depcreating asshole who deserved what he got. What if I end up like him, a cruel, heartless man that drives away the ones he’s supposed to cherish?” 

Tears well up in the corner of his golden eyes. “What if I do everything wrong and our son hates me? And what if one day, you wake up and realize that you’re–”

“Stop, that’s enough,” Phainon cuts him off abruptly, his arms tense and tight around Mydei. The man pauses. 

“Phainon?” he asks nervously when he finally notices the tightness of the pale-haired man’s jaw, the blistering fury in his pretty blue eyes.

“No, that’s never going to happen. You’re not your father, nor will you ever be.” He cups Mydei's cheek gently, his thumb wiping away the tear that finally falls from his eye. The blond scoffs weakly.

“How are you so sure about that? You’re just saying that because…” he trails off at the end, but Phainon knows what he means. 

“That’s not true,” he protests. “I’m not saying this just because I love you, but because I know you too. You’ve never been like him. You’re not cruel, bitter, or rude. You’re kind, patient, loving, and strong. And I know our kid is going to adore the hell out of you.” 

He presses his lips to Mydei’s forehead and rubs his back as he feels the baker curl in closer to his chest. “I know being a new parent sounds really intimidating right now, but I promise you, everything is going to be okay. As long as we have each other’s backs, we’ll keep moving forward. As a family.” 

He looks back at Mydei, who stares up at him silently, his shiny golden eyes burning holes into Phainon’s face. For a moment, he’s worried that he said something wrong again, but then the baker finally speaks up. 

“Phainon?” he says softly, his voice terribly small, a sharp contrast to his usual tone. 

“Yeah?” he responds in gentle encouragement. Mydei’s lips twitch and pull as he tries to force out whatever it is he wants to say.

“I–” he starts to say before stuttering to an abrupt halt. “I–” Mydei tries again, his brows furrowing in concentration. Whatever it is, it must be tough to get out, but he’s clearly determined. Phainon smiles slightly as a small inkling of realization seeps through. 

“Hey, it’s alright,” Phainon comforts reassuringly before tucking Mydei back safely into his arms. He can feel the baker stiffen at first before melting into his touch as Phainon presses a kiss to the top of his soft, straw colored hair. “You don’t need to push yourself, it’s alright. I know.” 

As Mydei starts to drift off again, Phainon begins to form a plan. 

After he knocks on the beautiful, shiny oak door, Phainon tries not to fidget nervously while he waits. He still anxiously swipes a free hand through his pale hair to try to tame it from the messy birdnest it’s in, while also juggling the large bouquet of sunflowers in his other hand. He suddenly straightens up again when he hears the faint footsteps coming down the stairs.

Gorgo smiles at him through the window before swinging open the door wide open, the mouthwatering scent of cinnamon rolls wafting out around him like a warm hug. “Phainon, it’s good to see you! Please come in!” Although he can still see the exhaustion in her eyes, her smile is sincere and bright as he steps inside. “Excuse the mess, I haven’t quite finished unpacking my things yet.” 

Phainon smiles and shakes his head as she leads them up the stairs and into the living room, where he sees several moving boxes still packed inside. “That’s not a problem at all. I’m just glad you agreed to meet with me today. I hope I’m not causing you too much trouble.” 

“Nonsense, this is no trouble at all! I’m just glad we can have a moment to talk by ourselves. He smiles before offering the bouquet. 

“I actually bought these for you as a housewarming gift, Mydei mentioned to me that sunflowers were your favorite.” 

“Oh,” Gorgo remarks softly as she takes the floral arrangement from him, her eyes soft as she cradles it to her chest. “Yes, they are. His father actually gifted me several large bouquets of them when we first started dating.”  She smiles sadly before fetching a tall glass out of the cupboard and filling it with water. 

“Thank you, they’re beautiful.” She caresses the petals with a look of nostalgia, and it sends a pang of guilt through Phainon’s heart. But fortunately, she quickly recovers and clears her throat, masterfully diverting the subject away from uncomfortable waters with a practiced smile. 

“The cinnamon rolls should be finished by now. Why don’t we have one with some tea and talk about what happened last night?” Before he arrived, Phainon had called her and given her a watered-down version of the events. Of course, she had panicked and at first wanted to rush over immediately to check on her son. However, Phainon worried that it would only stress and Mydei out even more after already having a restless night. 

Luckily, Hephaestion was more than happy to take Mydei out for a fun day while Phainon was gone, promising to call him if anything happened. As Gorgo takes the piping-hot buns out of the oven and begins to cut out their portion, Phainon finally tells her everything, starting from how he woke up to realize Mydei was missing to the moment when he discusses his uncertainties about the future. Gorgo listened intently until he finally finished.

“Oh, Mydeimos, my baby. He’s always been such a sensitive boy,” she sighs sadly after Phainon finally finishes. “When he was little, I always told him never to bottle up his emotions, that it’s healthy to feel scared or sad.” She pokes at her pastry, “I should have seen the signs before all of Eurypon’s ‘teachings’ took root.” Gorgo sighs heavily as she pushes her plate away, her appetite gone. “You know, he wasn’t always like that.” Phainon arches his eyebrow in surprise.

“When we first started dating, he was a complete gentleman. Sweet, intelligent, patient, all the girls in our class had some sort of crush on him,” Gorgo recalls with a small smile. “He walked me to all my classes, listened to my problems and gave advice, and did everything within his ability to make me smile and stay by my side. It was difficult not to fall in love with him at the time.” 

“Then what happened?” Phainon asks softly. Gorgo sighs. 

“I’m not quite sure, but I remembered there was one instance when Mydei had just turned two. He had said something to our son that had greatly upset him and made him cry.” Gorgo’s jaw tightens. “At first I thought he had just had a rough day at the office, and when I asked him about it later, when Mydeimos was already in bed, he apologized and said it wouldn’t happen again.” 

She pauses, her hands balling up into fists. “But even since then, people have told me that he takes up after me. He can be impatient at times, and a little gruff, but he has a good heart and he cares for the people in his life.”

“He really does,” Phainon agrees, his heart skipping a beat. “I’m so happy to have met him and to have him in my life. And I know our baby will be too.” Gorgo slowly gives him a warm, motherly smile. 

“You really love my son, don’t you, Phainon?” she asks rhetorically. He wordlessly nods. With that, the elegant blond woman gets up from her seat and walks over to a bookshelf where she grabs a small black box from the tallest ledge. She cracks it open to peer inside, as if to check if the contents are still there, before gently shutting it again. 

She walks back over to Phainon and holds it out in the palm of her hand. “This is for you. And for Mydeimos, when the time is right.” Silently, he takes it from her and opens it up to see a simple gold signet ring with what appears to be a trident design, featuring a horizontal line running through the three prongs.

Phainon’s eyes widen as he suddenly realizes what she means, “This is—”

“My old wedding ring. Eurypon allowed me to keep it at the beginning of our divorce settlement. The symbol is our family crest. I was originally going to give it to Mydei when he finally settled down,” she explains. “But I want you to have it and give it to him instead.” Phainon shakes his head and tries to hand it back.

He stutters, “I can’t accept this, it’s–” 

“No longer of use to me. Please, I insist.” Her eyes are kind but firm. “I know how much the two of you mean to each other, and when the time comes for you to ask the question finally, you’ll know.” 

“I–” Phainon is about to argue when the words suddenly won’t leave his tongue. He looks down at the ring again. The metal is shiny and polished, clearly well-maintained after so many years. He knows Mydei would love it regardless, but–marriage? 

“Thank you,” he finally replies, shutting the case shut regardless and slips it into his back pocket. “I’ll give it some thought.” Gorgo doesn’t say anything and smiles knowingly. She opens her mouth, about to ask him a question, when Phainon’s phone suddenly rings, startling the two. 

He pulls it out and almost forgets how to breathe when he sees Mydei’s name and profile picture flash across his phone screen. Had something happen, he couldn’t possibly be in labor yet, right? With his heart hammering away in his chest, Phainon hits the answer button.

“Hello?” he breaths nervously.

“Hey,” Mydei gruffly replies, his voice rough and slow like he had just woken up from a long nap. “Phainon–”

“Mydei, is everything okay? Where’s Hephaestion? Did your water break? Do you need me to take you to the hospital?” Phainon rambles on nervously. 

“Wha–no! I’m fine, you moron. Hephaestion dropped me back off at the apartment so I could take a nap,” the baker explains.

“Oh,” Phainon lets out a breath of relief. “Oh, okay. That’s good, did you have fun today?” 

“Yeah, we had brunch together, took the dog out for a walk, and did more baby shopping,” Mydei lists off. 

“His room is going to explode if we keep getting him things, ” Phainon chuckles.

“Well, he deserves to have all the nice things we see,” retorts Mydei. Phainon shakes his head in affectionate exasperation before suddenly recalling again.

“Oh, was there something you wanted from me then?” he asks curiously. There’s a long pause on Mydei’s end before he mumbles something under his breath. It’s hard to make out what he said clearly. ‘Wait, could you repeat that? I didn’t hear you properly.” Mydei hesitates before muttering again. Phainon presses the phone harder to his ear, “What?”

“I said–” Mydei growls louder this time, “When are you getting back? It’s already starting to feel lonely here, so hurry up.” He then abruptly hangs up, leaving Phainon stunned and amused. He hears Gorgo chuckle softly, her golden eyes bright with amusement. 

“I see he’s already feeling antsy.” She shakes her head before waving him off with another smile. “Go on, best not to keep him waiting. You know what he’s like when his temper is shorter.” 

Phainon can’t help but snort in agreement. He takes a warm cinnamon roll wrapped in napkins before thanking Gorgo again. He leaves with the pastry in his hand and a ring box in his pocket, and he feels lighter than air.

Chapter End Notes

So what did you think? Will Mydei finally tell Phainon how he feels??

Leave kudos and comments below if you liked the chapter, and I'll see you in the next one!😊

Chapter Summary

The day everyone has been waiting for is finally here 😉

Chapter Notes

Thank you so much for the support, I love you guys! I hope you enjoy this chapter because it's the one everyone's been looking forward to ❤️

I decided to add an extra chapter, maybe as an epilogue?? 😉

Mydei lets out a deep sigh as Phainon stubbornly clings to him, already wearing his scrubs even though he refuses to leave for work. “Phainon,” he exhales and tries to push him away again gently. The pale-haired man lets out a pitiful whine and tightens his grip around the pregnant man. “Phainon, you’re going to be late. You have to go to work,” the baker tries to reason.

“No, I don’t want to,” Phainon pouts, not unlike an exasperated child instead of a full-grown man. “I don’t want to leave you.” Mydei closes his eyes, breathes out of his nose, and slowly counts to ten in his mind to keep himself from punching the other man square in the jaw. As Apollo’s due date approaches rapidly, Phainon’s only gotten more needy. He follows Mydei everywhere he goes, never wanting to wander from his side.

Even if it was something small like going to the bathroom, Phainon was right behind him. Sure, it was cute, although annoying at first, but Mydei understood that the physician was worried and wanted to check that everything was still okay. Now it’s simply infuriating. He would be positive if Phainon could live in his skin, he would. 

The baker can feel the onset of a headache taking root as he tries to keep his cool. They’ve been stuck like this for the past ten minutes, and Mydei has half a mind just to throw Phainon out the front door when an idea suddenly pops into his head. He lets out a big, overexaggerated sigh and tugs at the firm arms still wrapped stubbornly around his neck. 

“Don’t make me call Hyacine to come and get you,” the baker threatens with an amused smirk that grows into a smile when Phainon stiffens and finally pulls away. He sticks his lower lip out in a pathetic, childlike pout.

“You’re so mean to me, Mydei, using our friend like that to try to force us apart,” he complains. Even though she’s a head shorter than both of them and seems like she wouldn’t hurt a fly with her sweet smile, Hyacine is a force to be reckoned with. As a nurse who has worked in almost every unit, both men knew she’s not someone to mess around with. 

Mydei scoffs as Phainon finally opens the door to leave, but he still hesitates over the threshold. “Go, we’ll be fine,” he ushers the other man completely out of the doorway, but the physician continues to stare at him longingly from the stoop like a kicked puppy.  Mydei sighs, “Phainon,” he repeats again with a hint of a warning in his voice. 

Luckily, he finally snaps out of his stupor with a sheepish grin. “Alright, I’m going. Just…” Phainon trails off. “Don’t have the baby without me.” Mydei pauses before scoffing. 

“Idiot, like I can control when I have our son. He’s not even due for at least a week,” he scolds. 

“I know that! But still…” Mydei sighs again, his expression softens as he takes a step towards the dejected man. He kisses Phainon softly, but swiftly pulls away again before the pale-haired man can latch onto him.

“You worry too much. I’m not completely alone. Ptlomey and Hephaestion are down in the shop. I can call them if I need anything.” Mydei then reaches down and gently rubs his heavily pregnant belly. “Now come say goodbye to your son before I change your mind.” The responding smile the baker gets is bright enough to rival the sun as Phainon takes a step towards him again. He kneels down to be level with Mydei’s stomach before speaking softly to their son, who’s awake and kicking this time. It’s almost as if he knew that his father was leaving. 

“H,i baby. Be a good boy for your mother and don’t give him too much trouble today, okay?” Phainon lightly presses his lips against the surface of Mydei’s protruding stomach, laughing when Apollo kicks back before standing up again to give Mydei one last kiss. “I love you, I’ll see you after work.” 

“Bye,” Mydei mutters back, watching as Phainon slowly walks down the stairs to the street where his car is parked. He flashes Mydei one last grin and a wave before getting in and driving off. Finally alone, the baker reenters their now-empty apartment and shuts the door behind them. He leans against the door and lets out a sigh. With his hand still resting on the baby bump, Mydei runs his free hand through his hair. 

He looks to the side and catches a glimpse of his reflection in the foyer mirror and scoffs. There’s crust in the corners of his eyes and a bit of dried drool on his cheek. His hair is dirty and mussed up from sleep, and he’s wearing one of their old, crusty university sweatshirts. Mydei blanches at his appearance, genuinely wondering how Phainon could find any of this attractive, especially when he’s extra grumpy in the early hours of the morning. 

His back already hurts, his feet are swollen, and he aches all over. Mydei wants to do nothing else except crawl back into bed, but given how big and swollen his belly is, it’s already hard enough to get back up on his own. So instead, he has to start his day. Since his exile from the cafe kitchen, Mydei finds himself becoming increasingly bored. 

At the very start, he’s relieved for the break and takes advantage of his new free time to organize the apartment, sort through the many baby things they’ve since procured, and sanitize all the necessary equipment they would need when Apollo comes. But now that everything is in place and neatly put away, Mydei finds himself growing more antsy. 

Luckily, he can still cook in his own kitchen, but it’s becoming difficult to navigate around with the baby. He has to use the bathroom every five minutes, has to be extra careful not to cut himself when using the knives, and even now, he hesitates about using the stovetop. 

Mydei lets out another long sigh before wandering into his guest room, which has been converted into the baby’s. There’s a small daybed in there, tucked into the corner across from the crib and practically swallowed by the mountain of stuffed toys eagerly awaiting Apollo’s arrival. He takes a seat in the rocking chair, closing his eyes as he gently swings back and forth. 

He cradles his heavy bump from underneath, caressing the taunt surface of his stretched skin and smiling slightly when he feels his son stir within him. “You’ve become more active now. Getting sick of being stuck inside me, huh?” he chirps kindly. He feels the baby punch as if in agreement. Mydei moves one hand to rest on the top. “I know, we’re almost there. Your father and I can’t wait to see you. So do your best and come out soon, okay?” 

Mydei ends up taking a short nap in the chair, his exhaustion finally winning him over, until Leo jumps into his lap with a purr. He looks down to see Bubbles napping peacefully by his feet. They still get up and dutifully follow him back out to the living room, where he starts to make himself a light midmorning snack when he checks his phone again to see that he’s already received a text from Phainon. 

I miss you already, the message reads, accompanied by several crying emojis. Mydei scoffs before he scrolls down to see the photo Phainon took, his head resting on a desk with a small pout on his lips. The baker rolls his eyes and sends back a short response. 

You’ll live, he then follows it up with a picture of his half-eaten yogurt. Can you swing by the grocery store and pick up some more? We’re almost out.

Of course, anything for you! 

Thanks, Mydei pauses, his fingers hovering over the keyboard. He starts to type out those damned words when Phainon beats him to it. 

Shoot, I gotta get back! Call me if anything happens! I love you ♡ υ˶˃ ﻌ ˂˶υ ♡ 

Dammit, even his emoticons are adorable. Mydei slams his phone face down, his cheeks warm and aflame. He inhales the rest of the yogurt, places the dirty dishes in the sink to soak, and wanders back into the bathroom to wash up. 

 He splashes water on his face, rinsing away the thin coat of oil on his face and the rest of the grogginess that still stubbornly clings to him. Then, leaning against his hands on the sink, Mydei finally slowly looks up at his reflection. 

How does Phainon do it, constantly telling Mydei he loves him? He makes it look so easy, but when the baker tries it himself, those three cursed words get clogged in his throat like a stubborn hair. Mydei scowls in frustration, golden eyes bright with annoyance, before he takes in a deep breath. 

“Phainon, I–” he attempts again, only to stop again. “I–” Why can’t he say it? What the hell is wrong with him? He grits his teeth, determined, and tries once more. “I…love you,” he finally manages to whisper weakly. What, is he some sort of school child who’s dealing with a crush? Still, despite how pathetic he finds the attempt, it’s progress to Mydei. 

Apollo kicks him, hard, as if he agrees with the baker. Letting go of the sink, Mydei reaches back to soothe the babe and coos. “I know, I’m just being stupid. It’s just—” he exhales heavily. “I’ve never been good at expressing my emotions; that’s more your father’s job.” Mydei chuckles as he walks back into the living room, wincing when he feels a now familiar cramping pain. 

Bailu reassured them that it was natural for Mydei to have contraction-like cramps near the end of his pregnancy as his body is “practicing for the real labor next week. Still, it’s not a pleasant experience. Mydei winces and braces himself, trying to relax again when his son punches him. 

Mydei sits down on the couch, his breath catching in his throat from the pain, just as Apollo starts to turn when another contraction passes through him, sudden and more painful. He hisses and lurches forward. Something’s not right. He looks around for his phone when Mydei remembers that he stupidly left it in the bathroom. 

Getting up and walking is the hardest thing he’s had to do on his own. He holds the wall for support as he hobbles. He’s almost there when he feels something trickle down his inner thighs. Mydei finally braces himself and looks down to see the growing puddle of liquid gathering under his feet. 

No, not now, it’s still early. He can’t–Phainon. Apollo. 

Mydei forces himself to grab his phone on the bathroom sink counter and blindly hits the first number he sees. As he listens to the sound of ringing on the other end, another contraction slams into him like a brick wall. Their baby is coming now. 

“Hello, Mydei?” Luckily, Hephaestion has always been fast at picking up the phone. “Are you okay?”

“Hospital,” Mydei manages to get out between gritted teeth. “I need to go to the hospital. My water just broke, the baby is coming.”

Phainon gets the news as he’s just wrapping up his lunch break. He’s washing his lunch box tupperware in the sink when he hears people running towards him. Alarmed, he looks up to see Castorice and Cipher, both out of breath and wide-eyed. “Hey guys, what’s going on?” 

“It’s Mydei, his water just broke. He’s in labor!” Phainon’s heart almost stops.

“What?!” 

“You need to go, he’s at the hospital!” He’s out the door before they could utter another word. He tries to keep it at a reasonable speed, but his foot never lets off the accelerator; he’ll have to deal with the potential of getting a speeding ticket, but that doesn’t matter. None of that matters except for Mydei and their son. 

By some miracle, he doesn’t meet any red lights or traffic, and he makes it to the hospital in record time. He runs to the front desk and demands Mydei’s room, where a pretty male nurse with long blond hair patiently directs him down the hall to their labor and delivery wing. 

He bursts into their room where Mydei and his mother are waiting. The baker’s face is pale and serious, his bangs plastered to his forehead with sweat. He grips the handrails on the side of the bed so tightly that his knuckles go white. Gorgo, who had been busy wiping her son’s forehead, looks up and gives Phainon a relieved smile. 

“Oh, good, you’re here just in time,” she says as Phainon makes his way to Mydei’s side. 

“How is he? How’s the baby?” he immediately asks as Mydei slowly turns to face him. 

“About four centimeters dilated, baby’s vitals are good,” she reports. Phainon lets out a sigh just as Mydei relaxes again, his expression tight with discomfort. Phainon hesitates but still reaches out to gently pet his dual colored hair. 

“You feeling alright?” he asks without thinking, instantly regretting it when Mydei shoots him a sharp glare. 

“I’m about to push a whole baby out of an opening that’s as big as a bagel, what do you think?” he shoots back sarcastically. Gorgo chokes a little as she tries to stifle back her giggle. Mydei, of course, has the grace to ignore his mother. Sensing that Phainon might need his help, she graciously lets him take her place next to Mydei. 

He offers the baker his hand to hold in support, trying not to wince when he feels the crushing pressure on his fingers when Mydei goes through another contraction. Phainon tries to take his mind off the pain in between waves by massaging his tense shoulders. When he tries to get to his lower back, Mydei flashes him a searing glare that forces Phainon back. He opens his mouth, about to admonish Phainon again, when another contraction hits, causing him to hiss in pain. 

Luckily, Bailu shows up again to check up on Mydei. As she does, the doctor asks him simple questions to which Mydei answers with simple grunts and one-word answers. 

“You’re progressing along nicely, at about six centimeters. It shouldn’t be too long now,” she encourages him kindly with a smile. “You’re also handling the pain pretty well, too. Most people would have started screaming bloody murder by now.”

“Well, I have a pretty high pain tolerance,” Mydei explains while crushing Phainon’s hand to dust. He tries not to whimper when the baker’s grip on his fingers tightens. Bailu glances at him before quickly hiding her amusement behind a polite cough. 

“I’ll check back in an hour, but please buzz our staff if something is wrong or if you need anything,” the doctor says before leaving again. Gorgo then gets up and asks Mydei if he wants something from the canteen downstairs.

“Pomegranates, if they have any,” he instantly replies. His mother complies and, after telling the couple that she will be back quickly, she leaves the two men alone for the first time since the start of Mydei’s labor. The blond man finally lets go of Phainon’s hand, letting him take the seat next ot the bed (Phainon would have preferred getting in next to Mydei, but decides against it to avoid losing his head, or any other precious body parts). 

“HSK, this is all your fault,” Mydei mutters while turning over to frown at the pale-haired man. 

“Oh, how come?” Phainon asks innocently after deciding to play along, both to serve as a distraction and just because, why not? 

“You jinxed it before you left this morning, like an idiot. You told me not to have the baby without you, and then this happens,” Mydei grunts, much to Phainon’s surprise. He bites the inside of his cheek to keep from smiling before replying. 

“Right, I did say that,” Phainon simply answers, his voice trembling slightly as he fights back the giggle. Mydei narrows his golden eyes in disapproval. “Sorry, I am really sorry. I didn’t mean for it to actually come true. We both know that was meant as a joke.” Mydei noticeably stiffens again, his jaw clenches as he resists the urge to yell as another contraction hits him.

Phainon offers his hand to Mydei again at once, bracing himself for the pain when the baker squeezes even harder. The pregnant man breathes heavily through his nose and squeezes his eyes shut. Phainon can’t help but feel a pang of guilt when he sees how uncomfortable it is. The physician gently rubs the back of Mydei’s hand with his thumb. 

“This baby has a sick sense of humor, then,” he scoffs after it passes. There’s a strange gleam in his eyes as Mydei relaxes again. But when Phainon is about to ask what is on his mind, Gorgo returns with a cup of pomegranate juice and a milk carton. She pours the milk into the juice, dying the once dark red drink pink. 

Mydei takes small sips of his favorite beverage, trying his best not to spill as the contractions get faster and stronger. Both Gorgo and Phainon do their best to help him through it, demonstrating breathing techniques and helping him adjust his position to rest more comfortably in the bed. He even tries to move around the room, but it proves to be too difficult to get up again. 

“Fuck!” he finally roars in pain when he tries to get onto his feet. Phainon guides him back down on the bed.  

About an hour and a half later, Bailu and her team came back, sterilized with their gloves and operating gown to check up on him again. Phainon almost forgets to breathe when she excitedly announces that Mydei is fully dilated and ready to go. The medics instantly move into position, and the physician is instructed to hold one of his legs while the other nurses hold the other. 

“Alright, mister Nikador, are you ready to start pushing?” she asks while putting on and adjusting her gloves. Mydei swallows nervously before slowly nodding. Phainon squeezes his hand again. 

“You got this, Mydei, I’m right here,” Phainon says reassuringly as he wraps his arm under Mydei’s knee and pulls it open. Mydei, under the spell of excruciating pain, turns to shoot him a burning scowl. 

“Of course you’re here! You’re the whole reason I’m here!” he spits out while his features scrunch up in pain. He even lets go of the physician’s hand to grab at Phainon’s hospital gown, yanking on it as he lets out a long and low drawn-out groan, an intense contraction running through his body. 

“Alright, push now!” Bailu instructs from her spot in front of Mydei. Gorgo, who’s holding Mydei’s other leg, flashes an apologetic smile at Phainon. Mydei strains, pushing so hard his face goes red until he falls back with an exhausted yell. 

“Mydei..” Phainon stutters while trying to untangle his fingers from the collar of his top. 

“And…push!” Bailu orders again as another contraction washes through Mydei’s body. He pushes harder than before, yelling with all his might. “Push!” The pattern continues, Mydei keeps exerting himself as tears run down his cheeks and his hair sticks to his face. He cries with each excruciating contraction but keeps going until Bailu excitedly announces, “Come on, I can see a head!” 

Mydei lets out a whimper before pushing once more. “There are the shoulders, and the arms! You’re doing great, keep going!” Phainon feels like he’s going to faint from excitement as their son continues to come. “Phainon, I need you here!” The good doctor orders sharply, jolting the pale-haired man into action. One of the nurses takes his place next to Mydei’s leg as Phainon dashes over to the end of the bed. 

It’s a strange but beautiful sight, but he dutifully follows Bailu’s instructions on catching the baby as he continues to slowly make his way into the world. He holds his hands together, and despite how they’re shaking, Phainon is determined. 

“Alright, we’re almost there! One last big push! Come on, you can do it, mister Nikador!” Bailu continues to cheer. Gathering up what is certainly the last of his strength, the baker braces himself up on the bed and with his biggest push, screams.

Their son falls into Phainon’s hands, letting out a shrill wail as he finally enters the world. Tears instantly well up in the physician’s light blue eyes as he cradles the tiny being with the most care in the world. The baby is bright red, wrinkly, and covered in a mixture of blood and amniotic fluid. He is the most beautiful thing Phainon has ever seen. His hair, although dirty and wet, is the same shade of blonde as Mydei’s.

“Would you like to cut the umbilical cord, mister Khlasana?” one of the nurses asks him while holding a large pair of scissors. He’s very reluctant about having to hand their son over to her, but he does it, watching very closely as he takes the long shears to the cord. The organ is spongy and surprisingly tough, but he manages to snip all the way through it eventually.

Once he’s done, the nurses move Apollo onto a changing table where they ever so carefully wipe him down and take his measurements, gently shushing him as he continues to cry. They then put him in a newborn diaper and a small blue hand-knit cap. They swaddle him in a blue and white striped blanket before finally handing him back to Phainon.

“Hello there, Apollo. It’s me, your papa. I can’t believe you’re finally here,” Phainon coos softly while gently rocking him back and forth. The baby’s sobs soften slightly at the sound of his voice. Phainon makes sure to walk gently back to Mydei’s side. 

Bailu and another doctor have just finished checking on Mydei’s vitals and were in the process of cleaning him up. Gorgo stays by his side, making sure he drinks all of his water while brushing away his damp hair from his face. She kisses and tightly squeezes her son while whispering soft words of praise. The baker is exhausted, resting heavily against his mother with his head on her shoulder. His eyes are almost closed, but when they spot Phainon and their baby, they shoot open again. 

He undoes his hospital gown a little more and holds his arms out for skin-to-skin bonding. Phainon sits down on the edge of the bed and carefully unwraps the blanket before transferring their son into his mother’s arms.

Apollo coos and whimpers in protest, but quickly settles down again when he rests against Mydei’s chest. Mydei sniffles, no longer fighting back the tears as their child nestles and squirms. “Apollo,” he whispers, so quiet and loving as he sweetly pets their son’s head. 

The babe strongly resembles Mydei, but when he cracks open one of his eyes, it’s an exact copy of Phainon’s icy blue ones.  Phainon can feel his throat start to swell with emotions again as he curls an arm around the two most important people in his life. He kisses the side of Mydei’s head just as he feels a tear trickle down his face. 

“You were incredible, I’m so proud of you,” he says sincerely. “I love you so much.” He then feels Mydei shift under his arm, turning his face up to lock eyes. “Mydei?” 

“I feel the same way. About you, I mean,” Mydei mumbles, barely audible. He still doesn’t say the words, but Phainon knows he means it. He swoops down to give the baker a slow and gentle kiss on the lips before Mydei pulls him in to lie down in the bed right next to him. 

Phainon falls asleep the happiest he’s ever been, with his new family tucked safely in his arms.
